why: 'Good morning' is a fixed greeting; 'Хорошее утро' (Good/Nice morning) is a literal word-for-word translation that does not exist as a Russian greeting.
'How are you?' is rendered as 'Как дела?' in Russian; 'Как ты есть?' is a word-for-word translation that sounds foreign and unnatural.
Russian does not use the verb 'есть' (to be) in the present tense predicate; 'Я есть хорошо' is an ungrammatical calque of English.
'Nice to meet you' as a greeting has the fixed Russian equivalent 'Приятно познакомиться'; 'Приятно встретить тебя' (nice to encounter you) is not the standard greeting phrase.
'See you later' is a farewell idiom; the Russian equivalent is 'До встречи' or 'До скорого'; 'Увижу тебя позже' is a literal translation that sounds unnatural as a parting phrase.
'Я нуждаюсь в помощи' is grammatically correct but overly formal and literary; 'Мне нужна помощь' is the natural everyday phrasing.
The Russian for 'What time is it?' is 'Который час?' or 'Сколько времени?'; 'Какое время это есть?' is an ungrammatical literal translation.
'Извините' is the correct imperative form used as an apology; 'Извиняй меня' uses the wrong aspect and form of the verb.
'Я не понимаю' uses the correct first-person indicative; 'понимай' is an imperative form and ungrammatical in this context.
The polite imperative is 'Повторите'; 'повторяйте' is an imperfective form that implies repeated action, which is incorrect here.
'помедленнее' is the natural comparative adverb; 'более медленно' is a formal analytical comparative that sounds stilted in everyday speech.
'Thank you very much' has the fixed Russian equivalent 'Большое спасибо' or 'Очень вам благодарен'; 'Спасибо очень много' is a word-for-word literal translation that does not work in Russian.
'You're welcome' as a response to thanks is 'Пожалуйста' in Russian; 'Ты приветствован' is a literal translation of 'you are welcomed' which does not serve this function.
'Я сожалею' is a formal expression of regret appropriate for official contexts; 'Прости' or 'Извини' is the natural everyday apology.
'ближайшая' is the superlative meaning 'nearest'; 'ближняя' means simply 'near' or 'close', and adding 'есть' (there is) is an ungrammatical calque.
'Я голоден' is the natural Russian expression for being hungry; 'У меня есть голод' (I have hunger) is a literal calque from English.
'Я хочу пить' (I want to drink) is the natural Russian equivalent; 'Я жаждущий' (I am thirsting) is an overly literary adjective not used in everyday speech.
'На улице' is the Russian idiom for 'outside' or 'outdoors'; 'Снаружи это холодно' uses 'снаружи' (outside of a building) and the unnecessary pronoun 'это'.
'Я устал' is the natural short-form predicative; 'Я являюсь усталым' uses the bookish copula 'являться' and is an unnatural calque of 'I am tired'.
'Good night' is 'Спокойной ночи' (literally 'of a peaceful night'); 'Хорошей ночи' (of a good night) is a literal word-for-word rendering that is not the established Russian farewell.
'I like' is 'Мне нравится'; 'Я люблю' means 'I love', which is a stronger feeling and changes the meaning.
'Weather' is 'погода' in Russian; 'метеорология' means meteorology (the science), which is a false cognate error.

src: I'll be back in five minutes.
bad: Я буду обратно в пять минут.
why: 'Я вернусь через пять минут' is the natural Russian; 'буду обратно в пять минут' is a literal translation of English word order that sounds unnatural in Russian.
'помогать' is the imperfective meaning ongoing help; 'помочь' (perfective) is correct for a one-time offer of assistance. 'Могу я' is also an unusual word order.
In Russian 'говорить по-русски' (speak in Russian) requires the prepositional prefix 'по-'; 'говорить русский' (speak Russian) treats language as a direct object incorrectly.
'ощущаю' and 'великолепно' are elevated, literary words; 'чувствую себя отлично' is the natural everyday expression.
'Я забыл ключи' is the standard everyday expression; 'позабыл о своих ключах' is more literary and implies forgetting entirely, which changes the nuance.
'I'm running late' means опаздываю (I am late); 'Я бегу поздно' (I'm running late) is a literal word-for-word translation with the physical meaning of running.
'Watch out' is an idiom meaning be careful; 'Наблюдай снаружи' (watch outside) is a nonsensical literal translation.
'Не проблема' is the natural colloquial equivalent; 'Никакой проблемы нет' is a more formal, verbose version not typical of casual speech.
'убеждён' means convinced, not uncertain; 'Я не убеждён' means 'I am not convinced', which has a different nuance from simple uncertainty.
'интересующее' is a participial form (the thing that is causing interest); 'интересно' is the short-form adjective used as a predicate, which is correct here.
'Я согласен' uses the correct short-form adjective; 'Я соглашаю' attempts to use 'соглашать' as a transitive verb without an object, which is ungrammatical in this construction.
'Дайте думать' or 'Дай подумаю' are natural Russian; 'Дайте мне думать' (let me be thinking) uses the imperfective aspect incorrectly and has unnatural word order.
'I'll do my best' maps to 'Я постараюсь' in Russian; 'Я сделаю моё лучшее' is a word-for-word translation that does not exist as an idiom in Russian.
'Ты отлично выглядишь' is the natural compliment; 'смотришься великолепно' is more literary and less common in everyday compliments.
'Я дома' is the natural conversational phrase; 'Я нахожусь в доме' (I am located inside the house) is overly formal and bureaucratic.
'Я позвоню' (perfective future) is correct for a single future call; 'буду звонить' (imperfective) implies repeated or ongoing calling which is not the intended meaning.
'Take care' as a farewell is 'Береги себя' in Russian; 'Бери уход' is a nonsensical literal translation of the English words.
The rejected translation adds 'человек' (person) which is not in the source and changes the statement from an in-context assertion to a personality description.
'I missed you' (emotionally) is 'Я скучал по тебе'; 'Я пропустил тебя' means I missed you (failed to see/catch you) which is the wrong sense.
'I'm on my way' means I am coming; 'Я нахожусь на своём пути' is a literal translation of 'I am on my path/way' that sounds stilted.
'Неважно' is the natural colloquial equivalent; 'Это не имеет значения' is a formal paraphrase more appropriate for written or official language.

'I need a moment' is 'Мне нужна минута' or 'Дай мне секунду'; 'нуждаюсь в моменте' is a literal translation using a formal register and the English word 'момент' as a false cognate for 'moment' of time.
'What's up?' is an informal greeting equivalent to 'How are you?'; 'Что наверху?' (what is up there/above?) is a nonsensical literal translation.
'проснулся' is the correct reflexive perfective for waking up; 'разбудился' does not exist as a valid reflexive form in standard Russian.
'свободен' is the short-form predicate adjective; 'свободный' is the full form used attributively, not predicatively in this type of sentence.
'Пойдём!' is the natural Russian invitation to go; 'Давай идём!' is understandable but less crisp and not the standard single-word equivalent.
'Я подумаю' uses the perfective future correctly; 'буду думать' (imperfective) implies prolonged thinking and does not convey a promise to consider something.

'Good luck!' is 'Удачи!' in Russian (genitive used as a wish); 'Хорошая удача!' (Good luck!) treats 'good' as an adjective, but Russian expresses this wish with the noun in the genitive without an adjective.
'How much?' for price is 'Сколько?' in Russian; 'Как много' literally means 'how many/much' but is not the standard question for price.

src: I'd like to try this on.
why: 'примерить' means to try on clothing; 'пробовать' means to taste or attempt in general and is not used for trying on clothes.

src: Do you have this in a larger size?
ok: Есть ли это в большем размере?
bad: Вы имеете это в более большом размере?
why: 'Есть ли это в большем размере?' is the natural question; 'Вы имеете это' is a literal calque of 'You have this' — Russian uses the existential 'есть' not 'иметь' for availability.
'Я возьму' (perfective future) is correct for a single act of purchase; 'буду брать' (imperfective) implies repeated taking.
'оплатить' (perfective) is correct for completing a payment; 'платить' (imperfective) implies ongoing payment and is less natural for a point-of-sale transaction.
'скидки' is the correct Russian word for discounts; 'дискаунты' is a non-standard borrowing not used in natural speech; 'иметь' is also the wrong verb for availability.
'чек' is the standard word for a sales receipt in Russian; 'квитанция' is a formal receipt for services, not typically used for retail purchases.

src: The fitting room is over there.
why: 'примерочная' is the standard Russian word for a fitting room; 'подгоночная комната' is a literal translation that does not exist as a set phrase.
'on sale' in the sense of discounted is 'по акции' or 'со скидкой'; 'на продаже' is a literal translation that means 'for sale' (available to buy), not discounted.
'закрыт' is the short-form passive participle used predicatively; 'закрытый' is the full-form adjective used attributively, which is incorrect in this predicate position.

src: I need to find a supermarket.
why: 'Мне нужно найти' is the natural everyday phrasing; 'Я нуждаюсь в нахождении' is a bookish, bureaucratic construction.
'доставка' is the word for delivery of goods to a customer; 'поставлять' means to supply goods (wholesale), which is a different commercial context.
'looking for' is 'ищу' (to search); 'смотрю за' means to watch over/supervise, which is a different meaning.
'дорого' is the correct Russian word for expensive; 'экспенсивно' is a non-existent borrowing from English.
'Можно вернуть?' is the natural informal question for returning merchandise; 'Могу я возвратить?' uses the more formal synonym 'возвратить'.
'не подходит' is the natural Russian for 'doesn't fit'; 'подгонять' means to drive/urge on, not fit clothing.
In a shop context 'a bag' at the register means 'пакет' (plastic/paper bag); 'сумка' is a handbag or reusable bag, which is a different item.
'очередь' is the standard Russian word for queue; 'куе' is a non-word — a phonetic Russification of 'queue' that does not exist in Russian.
'Is there a sale on?' means is there a promotional discount; 'Есть ли продажа включена?' (is a sale switched on?) is a nonsensical literal rendering.
'касса' is the checkout or cash register; 'кашир' is a non-standard phonetic borrowing and not the correct Russian word.
'обменять валюту' is the correct phrase for exchanging currency; 'сменить деньги' means to change money in the sense of getting change for a note, not currency exchange.
'срок годности истёк' is the correct Russian for 'expired product'; 'экспирован' is a non-existent Russification of 'expired'.
'марка' or 'бренд' are both used in Russian for a brand; 'бранд' is a non-standard phonetic borrowing without the correct Russian spelling 'бренд'.
'price tag' is 'ценник' in Russian; 'цена тег' is a literal two-word translation that does not exist as a term.
'вернуть деньги' is the natural Russian expression for getting a refund; 'рефунд' is a non-existent Russification of the English word.
'Это не тот размер' (this is not that size / not the right size) is the natural colloquial expression; 'неправильный' is technically correct but less natural in spoken Russian for clothing size.

src: Do you have a loyalty card?
why: 'карта лояльности' is the established Russian term for a loyalty card; 'карта верности' is a literal translation using 'верность' (faithfulness/fidelity) which is not the standard term.
'наличными' is the instrumental case used adverbially (pay with cash); 'наличные деньги' (nominative/accusative) treats cash as a direct object which is incorrect in this payment context.
'открывается' (reflexive, intransitive) correctly expresses the store opening on its own; 'открывает' (transitive) implies someone is opening it.

'Есть ли очередь покороче?' is the natural colloquial question; 'Существует ли более короткая очередь?' uses the formal verb 'существовать' (to exist) and analytical comparative, which are overly formal.
'цвет идёт' is the idiomatic Russian expression for a colour suiting someone; 'подходит' is understandable but less idiomatic for describing clothes.

src: I need to check the expiry date.
why: 'срок годности' is the established Russian term for expiry date; 'дата экспирации' is a non-standard borrowing not used in everyday Russian.

src: There's a queue at the checkout.
why: 'касса' is the Russian word for checkout; 'чекаут' is a non-standard borrowing not used in spoken Russian.

src: I'd like two kilograms of apples.
bad: Я хотел бы два килограмма яблок.
why: At a market or deli 'Мне два килограмма яблок' is the standard colloquial order phrasing; 'Я хотел бы' (I would like) is more formal and less typical for food market transactions.
'принимаете' is the standard word for accepting payment; 'акцептуете' is a formal financial term (accept a bill of exchange) not used for retail card acceptance.
'Можно меню?' is the natural colloquial restaurant request; 'Могу я видеть меню?' is a word-for-word translation of English that sounds stilted in Russian.
'сделать заказ' is the standard phrase for placing an order; 'ордерить' is a non-existent Russification of 'order'.
'bill' in a restaurant is 'счёт' in Russian; 'билл' is a transliteration of the English name, not a Russian word for a restaurant bill.
'out of stock' is 'нет в наличии' in Russian; 'вне запаса' is a literal translation that sounds unnatural and unidiomatic.
'Возьму две штуки' is the natural Russian for taking two items; 'два из этих' (two of these) is a literal preposition phrase that sounds foreign in Russian.
'Есть что-нибудь подешевле?' is the natural colloquial question; 'Вы имеете что-либо более дешёвое?' is a literal translation using 'иметь' (have as a property) instead of the existential 'есть'.

src: Where can I find dairy products?
bad: Где я могу находить молочные продукты?
why: 'находить' (imperfective) implies searching repeatedly; 'найти' (perfective) or the simpler 'Где молочные продукты?' is the natural question.
'Я просто смотрю' is the natural Russian for browsing; 'Я есть просто смотрящий' uses the copula 'есть' and a participial noun form, both of which are ungrammatical calques from English.

src: What floor is the electronics section on?
why: 'floor' in a building is 'этаж' in Russian; 'пол' means floor as in the physical surface underfoot, which is a false friend error.
'повреждено' is the correct Russian word for damaged; 'дамажировано' is a non-existent Russification of 'damaged'.

'размер поменьше' or 'поменьше размером' is the natural Russian phrasing; 'меньший один' is a word-for-word translation of 'a smaller one' that does not work in Russian (Russian does not use 'один' as a generic pronoun the same way).
'настоящая кожа' is the correct Russian for genuine leather; the rejected translation uses phonetic Russifications of English words.
'Keep the change' means 'сдачу не надо' (no need for change); 'держи изменение' (hold the change) is a nonsensical literal translation.
'выгодная покупка' or 'отличная сделка' is the natural Russian equivalent; 'баргейн' is a non-established borrowing not used in standard Russian.
'примерочная' is the standard Russian word for a changing/fitting room; 'изменяющаяся комната' (room that changes itself) is a nonsensical literal translation.
'репарации' in Russian means war reparations, not home repairs; 'ремонт' is the correct word for home repair.
'кран' is the Russian word for a tap or faucet; 'тап' is a phonetic borrowing that does not exist in standard Russian.

src: We need to clean the apartment.
why: 'убраться в квартире' is the natural expression for cleaning an apartment; 'клинить' is a non-existent verb in Russian (a Russification of 'clean').
'лифт' is the Russian word for elevator/lift; 'элеватор' in Russian refers to a grain elevator, not a building lift.

ok: Я захлопнул дверь и остался без ключей.
why: 'locked myself out' is an idiom for accidentally shutting the door on yourself; 'заблокировал себя снаружи' is a literal translation that sounds foreign.
'бойлер не функционирует' uses a formal technical verb; 'котёл не работает' is the natural everyday expression. Note: 'бойлер' is also used in Russian but 'котёл' is more universal.
'стиральная машина' is the established Russian compound for washing machine; 'вошинг машина' is a phonetic borrowing that does not exist in Russian.
'свет' is the correct Russian word for lights in a room; 'огни' refers to fires or decorative/theatrical lights, not household lighting.
'аренда' is the standard Russian word for rent; 'рент' is a non-established borrowing not used in everyday Russian.
Russian uses the possessive 'У нас есть' (we have) rather than 'иметь' (to own/have); 'Мы имеем шумных соседей' is a literal English calque.
'крыша' is the Russian word for roof; 'руф' is a phonetic borrowing that does not exist in standard Russian.

src: I need to fix the sink.
why: 'починить раковину' correctly uses both Russian words; 'зафиксировать синк' uses 'зафиксировать' (to fasten/fix in place) which is wrong, and 'синк' is not a Russian word.
'окна' is the Russian word for windows; 'виндоуз' is an English phonetic borrowing not used for household windows.

src: I need to take out the rubbish.
why: 'мусор' is the standard Russian word for rubbish/garbage; 'рубиш' is a phonetic borrowing that does not exist in Russian.
'садику' (сад, garden) is the correct Russian word; 'гарден' is a phonetic borrowing that does not exist in Russian.
'не закрывается на замок' is the natural expression for a door that won't lock; 'не будет блокироваться' is a future-tense literal translation that is unnatural in this context.
'отопление' is the Russian word for central heating; 'хитинг' is a non-existent Russification of 'heating'.
'сантехник' is the Russian word for plumber; 'плюмбер' is a non-standard borrowing not used in Russian.
'Пробки выбило' is the Russian idiom for a blown fuse (colloquial); 'предохранитель взорвался' (the fuse exploded) is a literal rendering that sounds alarming and is not the standard expression.
'пол' is the Russian word for floor; 'флор' is a phonetic borrowing that does not exist in Russian.

src: I need to repaint the walls.
why: 'покрасить' is the correct Russian verb for painting walls; 'перепейнтовать' is a non-existent Russification of 'repaint'.
'пожарная сигнализация' or 'датчик дыма' is the Russian term; the rejected translation uses a series of phonetic English borrowings that do not exist in standard Russian.

src: I live on the third floor.
why: 'floor' (storey) is 'этаж'; 'пол' means the surface of the floor, not a building storey. This is a false friend error.
'квартира' is the Russian word for flat/apartment; 'флэт' is a phonetic borrowing not used in standard Russian.
'трубы' is the Russian word for pipes; 'пайпы' is a phonetic borrowing not used in standard Russian.
'ипотека' is the established Russian loanword for mortgage; 'мортгэйдж' is a phonetic borrowing from English not used in Russian.
'Свет отключили' is the natural Russian for a power outage; 'пауэр' is a non-standard borrowing not used in this sense.
'разобрать вещи' (sort through/clear out things) is the natural Russian equivalent; 'деклаттерить' is a non-existent Russification of 'declutter'.

src: Lock the door when you leave.
ok: Закрой дверь на ключ, когда уходишь.
why: 'закрой на ключ' is the correct Russian phrase for locking a door; 'локни' is a non-existent Russification of 'lock'.
'ремонт' is the natural Russian word for renovation; 'реновирован' is a Russification of 'renovated' that sounds foreign, and 'флэт' is not standard Russian.
'У нас общая кухня' is the natural Russian; 'шерить' is a non-standard borrowing from 'share' not used in Russian speech.
'звонок' is the Russian word for a doorbell; 'дорбелл' is a non-existent phonetic borrowing.
'занавески' or 'шторы' is the Russian word for curtains; 'кёртины' is a phonetic borrowing not used in Russian.
'места для хранения' is the correct Russian phrase for storage space; 'сторадж спейса' uses phonetic borrowings that do not exist in Russian.

src: We need to fumigate the flat.
why: 'дезинсекция' is the established Russian term for pest fumigation; 'фумигировать' is a technical borrowing less used in everyday speech, and 'флэт' is not standard Russian.
'ведро для мусора' or 'мусорное ведро' is the Russian term for a rubbish bin; 'бин' is a phonetic borrowing not used in Russian.

src: I need to do the dishes.
why: 'do the dishes' means wash the crockery; 'делать блюда' (make dishes/food) is a literal translation that means cooking, not washing up.
'пропылесосить' is the correct Russian verb for vacuuming; 'вакуумировать' means to create a vacuum in a scientific/industrial sense, not to vacuum clean.
'с полной мебелью' or 'полностью меблирована' is the Russian expression; 'фёрнишед' is a phonetic borrowing that does not exist in Russian.
'холодильник' is the Russian word for fridge; 'фридж' is a non-standard phonetic borrowing not used in Russian.
'вытри' is the correct perfective imperative; 'протри' means to wipe through or polish a surface, which is a different action.

src: The key is under the mat.
why: 'мат' in Russian primarily means a profanity or a wrestling mat, not a doormat; 'коврик' is the correct word for a doormat.
'подвал' is the Russian word for basement; 'бейсмент' is a phonetic borrowing not used in standard Russian.

src: The internet connection is poor here.
why: 'плохой интернет' is the natural colloquial phrase; 'интернет коннекция' mixes Russian with an English borrowing that is not standard.
'Mind your head' is a warning about a low ceiling; 'Смотри за своей головой' (watch your head) is a literal translation that implies watching over one's head rather than ducking.
'overlooking' a view in Russian is expressed as 'вид на' (a view of/onto); 'квартира смотрит на парк' (the flat looks at the park) anthropomorphises the flat in an unnatural way.

src: The neighbours are very noisy at night.
bad: Соседи являются очень шумными в ночное время.
why: 'соседи очень шумят по ночам' is the natural colloquial phrasing; 'являются очень шумными в ночное время' uses the bookish copula 'являться' and formal time expression.
'переезжать' is the correct Russian verb for moving house; 'мувиться' is a non-existent Russification of 'move'.

src: The attic is full of old stuff.
why: 'чердак' is the Russian word for attic; 'аттик' is a phonetic borrowing not used in standard Russian.

src: The front door needs a new lock.
bad: Фронт дор нуждается в новом локе.
why: 'входная дверь' is the Russian for front door; the rejected translation uses phonetic borrowings ('фронт дор', 'локе') that do not exist in Russian.
The correct Russian spelling of the loanword is 'офис' (single f); 'оффис' is a misspelling.
'встреча' or 'совещание' are the natural Russian words for a work meeting; 'митинг' in Russian specifically refers to a political protest meeting.
'у меня срок сдачи' is the neutral Russian phrase; while 'дедлайн' is used in Russian, 'на дедлайне' is less established; the phrase 'у меня горит срок' is more natural.
'электронное письмо' or 'письмо' is the natural Russian for email; 'имейл' is used but 'послал' (past tense of 'послать') has an impolite connotation in Russian.
'распечатать' is the correct Russian verb for printing a document; 'принтировать' is a non-standard Russification of 'print'.
'повысили' is the natural Russian verb for getting promoted; 'промотировать' is a Russification of 'promote' that sounds foreign.
'got fired' in employment means was dismissed; 'сожгли' (burned) is a literal translation of the verb 'fire' in its physical sense.
'calling in sick' is the idiom for reporting absence due to illness; 'звоню больным' (I'm calling while sick) is a literal rendering that misses the fixed English idiom.

src: We have a team meeting every Monday.
ok: У нас каждый понедельник собрание команды.
bad: Мы имеем тим митинг каждый понедельник.
why: Russian uses possessive 'У нас есть' not 'иметь'; 'митинг' in Russian means political protest; 'тим' is a Russification of 'team'.

src: I need to update my CV.
why: 'резюме' is the Russian word for CV/resume; 'СВ' is the abbreviated English acronym not used in Russian. 'СВ' in Russian is a sleeper train compartment.
'кондиционер' is the Russian word for air conditioner; 'эйр-кондишнированным' is a phonetic borrowing and compound that does not exist in standard Russian.
'работать из дома' uses 'из' (from) which is the correct preposition; 'от дома' means from the house in a spatial sense and is incorrect for describing remote work.
'on track' is the idiom meaning proceeding as planned; 'идёт по плану' is the natural Russian equivalent; 'на треке' is a literal translation using the English word.
'перенесём встречу' is the correct Russian for rescheduling; 'рискедьюлим' is a non-existent Russification of 'reschedule'.
Russian expresses possession with 'у меня есть' not 'иметь'; 'я имею презентацию' is a calque of the English 'I have a presentation'.

src: The printer is out of ink.
why: 'вне чернила' is a nonsensical literal rendering of 'out of ink'; 'закончились чернила' (the ink ran out) is the natural Russian expression.

src: I need to fill in this form.

src: I need to hand in my report.

src: The boss wants the numbers by noon.
why: 'шеф' or 'начальник' are the natural Russian words for boss; 'цифры' means figures/numbers; 'нумберсы' and 'нуну' are non-existent Russifications.
'сверхурочно' is the established Russian adverb for overtime work; 'овертайм' is less standard in formal written Russian.

src: This is above my pay grade.

src: I have a job interview tomorrow.
why: 'собеседование' is the established Russian word for a job interview; 'джоб интервью' is a non-standard borrowing from English.

'touch base' is the idiom meaning to briefly contact someone; 'свяжемся' (let's get in touch) is the natural Russian equivalent; 'потрогаем базу' (let's touch the base physically) is a nonsensical literal rendering.

src: We need to be on the same page.
ok: Нам нужно прийти к единому пониманию.
bad: Нам нужно быть на одной странице.
why: 'on the same page' is the idiom for having a shared understanding; 'прийти к единому пониманию' is the natural Russian equivalent; 'на одной странице' (on one page) is a literal rendering that does not convey the idiom.

src: I need to sign off on this.
bad: Мне нужно подписать офф на этом.
why: 'sign off on' is the idiom for formally approving something; 'утвердить' is the natural Russian equivalent; 'подписать офф' is a literal rendering using English words.
'behind schedule' is 'отстаём от графика'; 'за расписанием' (behind the schedule spatially) is a literal rendering of the preposition 'behind'.

src: I'll set up a conference call.
why: 'организую звонок-конференцию' uses natural Russian; 'сетапну конференс колл' uses non-standard Russifications of all three English words.
'nailed' in this context means did excellently; 'прибили гвоздями' (nailed with nails) is a nonsensical literal rendering of the English slang.
'У меня болит голова' is the natural Russian expression for having a headache; 'я имею головную боль' is a literal calque using 'иметь' which is incorrect here.

src: I need to see a doctor.
why: 'Мне нужно к врачу' is the natural elliptical Russian expression; 'видеть доктора' (to see the doctor visually) is a literal calque of the English.
'скорая помощь' (скорая) is the Russian term for ambulance; 'позвоните' can mean call but 'вызовите' (summon) is more natural for emergency services; 'амбуланс' is a phonetic borrowing.

src: Take two tablets twice a day.
ok: Принимайте по две таблетки два раза в день.
bad: Берите два таблета дважды в день.
why: 'таблетки' (feminine) is the correct gender; 'таблета' is a non-standard masculine form; 'принимать лекарство' (take medicine) is the medical collocation, not 'брать'.
'температура' is the correct Russian word for temperature; 'темпера' in Russian is a type of paint (tempera), which is a false cognate.

src: I need to take my blood pressure.
bad: Мне нужно брать моё кровяное давление.
why: 'take blood pressure' is the English idiom; in Russian it is 'измерить давление' (measure blood pressure); 'брать моё кровяное давление' is a literal word-for-word rendering.
'фармация' means the science of pharmacy, not a pharmacy shop; 'аптека' is the correct Russian word for a pharmacy/chemist.
'похудеть' (perfective) is the correct Russian verb for losing weight as a goal; 'терять вес' (imperfective) implies ongoing weight loss without the sense of a goal.
'выздоравливаю после простуды' is the correct Russian; 'рекаверинг' is a non-existent Russification and 'холодного' (cold as an adjective) is the wrong word for a cold (illness).
'У меня болит горло' (my throat hurts) is the natural Russian expression; 'болезненное горло' (sore/painful throat as adjective) is grammatically correct but less natural in spoken Russian.

src: I have an appointment with the dentist.
why: 'запись к стоматологу' is the natural Russian for a dental appointment; 'аппойнтмент' and 'дентист' are non-standard Russifications.
'У меня болит спина' is correct; 'бэк' and 'хёртс' are non-existent Russifications of English words.
'отдохнуть' is the correct Russian verb for resting; 'рест' is a phonetic borrowing that does not exist as a Russian word.

'Я принимаю лекарства' (I take medicines) is the natural Russian; 'нахожусь на медикации' is a literal translation using a borrowing not standard in Russian.

src: I need to get a blood test.
ok: Мне нужно сдать кровь на анализ.
why: 'сдать кровь на анализ' is the idiomatic Russian expression for getting a blood test; 'получить тест крови' is a literal translation of 'get a blood test'.

src: My laptop is out of battery.

why: 'Заботливый' means caring/attentive; 'careful' is a different quality.

bad: To me it is boring without you.
why: 'Мне скучно без тебя' means I miss you; literal rendering 'boring without you' is wrong.

src: Они познакомились год назад и уже женились.
ok: They met a year ago and have already got married.
why: Second clause about getting married dropped.

bad: A black cat ran between them.
why: 'Пробежала чёрная кошка' means something drove a wedge between them; the literal version is nonsensical in English.

ok: She is very attentive to those around her.
bad: She is very attentive to the surrounding.
why: 'Окружающие' refers to people; 'the surrounding' is typically used for environment, not people.

ok: He does not keep his word.
bad: He does not hold his word.
why: English collocation is 'keep one's word', not 'hold one's word'.
'Найти общий язык' idiomatically means to find common ground.

src: Он добился её руки и сердца.
ok: He won her hand and heart.
bad: He achieved her hand and heart.
why: 'Добился' in courtship context means 'won'; 'achieved' is non-idiomatic here.

ok: Send me the photos from the party!
bad: I entreat you to transmit to me the photographic images from the social gathering!
why: Friendly message uses informal imperative, not elevated formal phrasing.
'Gave birth to' is the correct English expression; 'borned' is non-standard.

ok: Her parents are against their relationship.
bad: Her parents are against their relations.
why: 'Отношения' in romantic context is 'relationship', not 'relations'.

src: Они провели вечер вместе и разговаривали до рассвета.
ok: They spent the evening together and talked until dawn.
why: Second clause about talking until dawn dropped.

src: У них нет детей, хотя оба очень хотят.
ok: They have no children, although both really want them.
why: Concessive clause about their desire for children dropped.
'Давние знакомые' = old acquaintances; 'long-time knowers' is a non-existent calque.

ok: She has a large, close-knit family.
bad: At her there is a big friendly family.
why: 'У неё' requires 'she has'; 'дружная семья' is a close-knit family, not merely a friendly one.

ok: His relatives live in the countryside.
bad: His relatives live in the village.
why: 'Деревня' often means the countryside/rural area in general usage; 'village' is more specific.

ok: They made up after the argument.
why: 'Помирились' = made up; 'reconciled' is more formal; 'squabble' downplays 'ссора'.
'Одна' in relationship context means single, not physically alone.
Specific people require a possessive or article; 'Parents' without 'his' is indefinite.
'Elder' is more formal/literary; 'older' is the standard everyday comparative.
'Общаются' means communicate generally; 'correspond' implies letters/email specifically.
'Ревнивый' means jealous (in relationships); 'envious' is a different emotion (wanting what others have).

src: Он встречается с Машей уже год.
ok: He has been dating Masha for a year.
bad: He meets with Masha already a year.
why: 'Встречаться' in relationship context is 'to date'; ongoing state requires present perfect continuous.
'Чувства' in emotional context means feelings; 'senses' refers to the five senses.

src: Бабушка испекла пирог для всей семьи.
ok: Grandmother baked a pie for the whole family.
bad: The grandmother has baked pie for whole family.
why: Article missing before 'pie' and 'whole family'; past simple preferred for completed one-time action.
'Деликатная' about a person means tactful/considerate; 'delicate' implies fragility.

ok: We haven't seen each other in a long time.
why: Russian perfective negation requires English present perfect with negation.
'Подруга' means female friend, not girlfriend; 'верная' here means loyal.
'Случайно' means by chance/accidentally; 'casually' describes manner not randomness.

src: Он предложил ей руку и сердце.
bad: He offered her his hand and heart.
why: 'Предложить руку и сердце' means to propose marriage; the English idiom is simply 'proposed to'.

src: Мы отмечаем годовщину свадьбы каждый год, и это очень важно для нас обоих.
ok: We celebrate our wedding anniversary every year, and it is very important to both of us.
bad: We celebrate our wedding anniversary every year.
why: Second clause expressing personal importance dropped.
'Very' cannot modify a verb; 'really' or 'greatly' required.
English reflexive is not used with 'argue/quarrel'; 'quarrel themselves' is ungrammatical.

src: Она сказала ему правду, потому что любила его.
ok: She told him the truth because she loved him.
why: Causal clause 'потому что любила его' dropped entirely.

ok: I enjoy walking in the forest.
bad: To me it is pleasing to walk in the forest.
why: Dative 'мне нравится' requires 'I enjoy'.

bad: On the street there is strong frost.
why: Russian weather expression requires English impersonal 'it is cold'.
'Идёт снег' is the Russian impersonal; English requires 'it is snowing'.

ok: The leaves turned yellow earlier than usual.
bad: Leaves have yellowed earlier than usual.
why: Definite article required before 'leaves' in this context; past simple preferred for a completed seasonal change.

ok: The weather changed a few hours ago.
bad: The weather has changed a few hours ago.
why: Specific past time reference 'ago' requires simple past, not present perfect.

ok: The river became shallow due to the drought.
bad: The river became low due to the drought.
why: 'Обмелела' describes a river becoming shallow; 'low' is imprecise.

ok: The stars are shining brightly tonight.
why: Night observation uses 'tonight'; definite article required before 'stars'; present continuous for ongoing act.
'Гроза' is a thunderstorm, but 'approaching' is more precise than 'coming closer'; 'storm' is acceptable but 'thunderstorm' is not wrong — this is a word-choice marginal case.

bad: I require you to don your headwear immediately!
why: Practical everyday command uses direct imperative, not formal decree.

ok: Close the window — there's a draught!
bad: I cordially request that you seal the window aperture, as an unpleasant air current is present.
why: Casual home instruction uses short imperative, not ornate formal prose.
Classic philosophical expression has a fixed English rendering.

ok: You can't make an omelette without breaking eggs.
bad: When the forest is cut, chips fly.
why: Russian proverb about collateral damage maps to English 'can't make an omelette without breaking eggs'.

ok: In the mountains it is cold even in summer.
bad: In mountains cold even in summer.
why: Definite article required before 'mountains'; impersonal 'it is' required for weather.

src: Весна пришла поздно в этом году.
bad: Spring has arrived late this year.
why: Specific year reference requires simple past; present perfect is incorrect with 'this year' when the event is complete.

ok: The willow weeps by the river.
bad: The iva weeps by the river.
why: 'Ива' must be translated as 'willow', not left as 'iva'.

ok: Dew covered the grass early in the morning.
bad: The dew covered the grass early in the morning.
why: Generic natural phenomenon 'роса' takes no article in English as a general reference.

ok: The wildfire engulfed hundreds of hectares.
bad: The forest fire embraced hundreds of hectares.
why: 'Охватил' for fire means engulfed; 'embraced' is non-standard for fires.

ok: The nature reserve is protected by the state.
bad: The reservation is protected by the state.
why: 'Заповедник' is a nature reserve; 'reservation' is a false friend (Native American or hotel context).
'Мягкий' about climate means mild, not soft.

src: Паводок затопил деревню, и жителей эвакуировали.
ok: The flood inundated the village, and the residents were evacuated.
why: Second clause about evacuation dropped.

ok: The wind died down by evening.
bad: The wind calmed to the evening.
why: 'Стих' for wind means died down; 'к вечеру' is 'by evening', not 'to the evening'.
'Рассеялся' for fog means lifted; 'к полудню' is 'by noon'.

ok: Nature recovers slowly after a fire.
why: 'Восстанавливается' is 'recovers'; 'restores' is transitive and implies an agent acting on something.

ok: Mountain air is clean and fresh.
bad: The mountain air is pure and fresh.
why: General statement about mountain air uses no article; 'чистый' is clean not pure in everyday air context.

src: На дереве свили гнездо две птицы.
ok: Two birds built a nest in the tree.
bad: On the tree two birds wove a nest.
why: 'Свить гнездо' means to build/make a nest; birds build nests, not weave them in standard English.

src: Несмотря на дождь, дети пошли гулять, и промокли насквозь.
ok: Despite the rain, the children went out to play and got soaked through.
bad: Despite the rain, the children went out to play.
why: Second clause about getting soaked dropped.

src: Осень наступает раньше в этом году.
ok: Autumn is coming earlier this year.
why: 'Наступает' for seasons means arrives/comes; 'attacks' is a false calque.

bad: The lake covered itself with ice.
why: 'Покрылось льдом' has the natural English equivalent 'froze over'.

ok: The ecology of the area deteriorated because of the factory.
bad: The ecology of the area worsened due to the plant.
why: 'Завод' can be factory or plant; 'factory' is more precise in pollution context; 'worsened' is slightly informal.

src: Медведь впал в спячку на зиму.
ok: The bear went into hibernation for the winter.
bad: The bear fell into hibernation for winter.
why: 'Went into hibernation' is the natural collocation; definite article 'the winter' required.
Ongoing event at the moment uses present continuous; 'erupts lava' sounds like a general fact.

ok: The moon is reflected in the water.
bad: The moon reflects in the water.
why: The moon doesn't actively reflect; it is reflected — passive voice required.

ok: The drought caused massive damage to the harvest.
bad: The drought inflicted enormous harm on the harvest.
why: 'Нанесла урон' in agricultural context maps to 'caused damage'; 'inflicted harm' is more formal/military.

bad: Migratory birds flew away to the south.
why: Definite article required; 'flew south' is the natural idiom over 'flew away to the south'.

ok: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
bad: The Earth rotates around the Sun.
why: 'Вращается вокруг' for orbital motion means revolves; 'rotates' means spinning on its own axis.
Stative adjective 'impressive' preferred over active verb 'impresses' for describing scenery.

src: На горизонте появились тёмные тучи, и вскоре начался ливень.
ok: Dark clouds appeared on the horizon, and a downpour soon began.
bad: Dark clouds appeared on the horizon.
why: Second clause about the downpour dropped.

src: Природа прекрасна во всех своих проявлениях.
ok: Nature is beautiful in all its manifestations.
bad: The nature is beautiful in all its manifestations.
why: Abstract noun 'nature' used in a general sense takes no article.
Stative description prefers adjectival predicate 'is invigorating' over simple active verb.

ok: The taiga is the lungs of the planet.
bad: The taiga is the lights of the planet.
why: 'Лёгкие' as a metaphor means lungs, not lights.

ok: It is raining cats and dogs.
bad: The rain pours as from a bucket.
why: Russian idiom 'льёт как из ведра' maps to English 'raining cats and dogs'.

ok: After the rain, the air became fresher.
bad: After rain air became more fresh.
why: Definite article required for specific rain event; comparative 'fresher' preferred over 'more fresh'.

ok: A moose stepped out onto the road.
bad: The elk walked out on the road.
why: 'Лось' in North American context is a moose; preposition 'onto' preferred; 'walked out on' is a phrasal verb with different meaning.

ok: The glacier is melting due to global warming.
bad: The glacier melts because of global warming.
why: Ongoing process uses present continuous; 'due to' is the standard collocation with 'global warming'.
'Рассвет наступил' — dawn broke is the natural English idiom; 'attacked' is a false calque.

ok: The weather forecast calls for snow.
why: 'Прогноз погоды' is weather forecast; 'prognosis' is a medical false friend; 'promises' is non-standard — 'calls for' is idiomatic.

ok: The sun set below the horizon.
bad: The sun went for the horizon.
why: 'Зайти за горизонт' means to set below the horizon; 'went for' is nonsensical.

src: Снежная буря накрыла регион, и дороги были закрыты на сутки.
ok: A snowstorm swept over the region, and the roads were closed for a day.
bad: A snowstorm swept over the region.
why: Second clause about road closures dropped.

ok: Mosquitoes are especially active at dusk.
bad: Mosquitoes bite especially actively in the evening.
why: 'Вечером' in outdoor insect context often refers to dusk; 'bite actively' is non-idiomatic.

src: Природа даёт нам всё необходимое, но мы должны её беречь.
ok: Nature gives us everything we need, but we must take care of it.
bad: Nature gives us everything we need.
why: Second clause about conservation duty dropped.

bad: To me it is pleasing to watch football.
why: Dative 'мне нравится' rendered word-for-word; 'I enjoy' required.

bad: He is engaged in sport every morning.
why: 'Занимается спортом' = does sports/exercises; 'engaged in sport' is overly formal.

src: Команда забила гол на последней минуте.
ok: The team scored a goal in the last minute.
bad: Team struck a goal on last minute.
why: Articles required; 'scored a goal' is the correct collocation; 'on last minute' should be 'in the last minute'.

src: Он бежит марафон уже третий раз.
ok: He is running a marathon for the third time.
bad: He runs the marathon already third time.
why: Dative-style rendering; natural English uses present continuous + ordinal with 'for'.

src: Они выиграли чемпионат два года назад.
ok: They won the championship two years ago.
bad: They have won the championship two years ago.
why: Specific past time reference 'ago' requires simple past, not present perfect.
'Спортсмен' in modern context translates as athlete; 'sportsman' implies hunting/fishing in British usage.

ok: The coach is demanding of his players.
bad: The trainer is demanding to his players.
why: Team sport leader is a 'coach'; 'demanding of' is the correct collocation, not 'demanding to'.

bad: I implore you not to surrender under any circumstances!
why: Motivational cheer uses direct short imperative, not formal plea.

bad: I urge you to conduct yourself in an honourable manner during the contest!
why: Sports sportsmanship reminder uses short imperative, not formal admonition.

ok: The game is not worth the candle.
bad: The game is not worth candles.
why: Fixed English idiom 'the game is not worth the candle' — singular 'the candle' required.
Russian proverb maps to 'might makes right' or 'winners write history'; the literal rendering is unusual.

ok: He is fighting for first place.
why: 'Бороться' in competition context is 'fighting for'; 'struggles' implies hardship rather than competition.

ok: The final takes place on Saturday.
bad: The final will be taking place on Saturday.
why: Scheduled event uses simple present; progressive form is awkward here.

ok: The stadium holds fifty thousand spectators.
bad: The stadium contains fifty thousand spectators.
why: 'Вмещает' for venues means holds/seats; 'contains' implies the spectators are already inside.

ok: The fans are chanting their player's name.
bad: The fans scan the name of their player.
why: 'Скандировать' means to chant; 'scan' is a false friend.

src: Он установил рекорд на прошлой неделе.
ok: He set a record last week.
bad: He established a record last week.
why: 'Установил рекорд' = set a record; 'established' is non-idiomatic in sports context.
Score expressed as 'three to one' without preamble; 'with score' is non-standard.

ok: The referee sent the player off.
bad: The judge removed the player from the field.
why: Sports official is a 'referee'; 'sent off' is the correct sporting idiom; 'judge' is a false friend.

src: Концерт прошёл на ура, и все уходили счастливые.
ok: The concert was a great success, and everyone left happy.
bad: The concert was a great success.
why: Second clause about audience leaving happily dropped.

src: Несмотря на травму, он продолжил игру.
ok: Despite the injury, he continued playing.
why: Concessive clause 'несмотря на травму' dropped.
'Увлекаться' for a hobby means to be into something; 'fascinated by' implies intellectual wonder rather than regular practice.

ok: The film ran for two hours.
why: 'Шёл' for a film's duration means ran for; 'went' is non-standard.
'Пьеса' in theatre is a play; 'piece' implies music; 'performed' preferred over 'played' for theatre.
'Коллекционирует' is the verb 'collects'; 'collections' is a noun.

src: Он записывает музыку в свободное время.
ok: He records music in his free time.
bad: He writes music in free time.
why: 'Записывает музыку' = records music (studio/digital); 'writes' implies composition; 'in his free time' needs possessive.

ok: The fans supported the team throughout the game.
bad: The supporters held the team through the game.
why: 'Поддерживали' = supported; 'held' is a mistranslation of the Russian stem.

ok: The match was postponed due to bad weather.
bad: The match was transferred due to bad weather.
why: 'Перенесли' in scheduling context means postponed; 'transferred' is the false friend calque.

ok: He is an artist by vocation.
bad: He is an artist by calling.
why: 'Призвание' maps more naturally to 'vocation'; 'calling' is a slightly religious variant but acceptable — the better-natural option is 'vocation'.

src: Она посещает театр раз в месяц.
ok: She goes to the theatre once a month.
bad: She visits theatre once in a month.
why: 'Once a month' is the correct frequency expression; 'visits theatre' needs definite article.

src: Победа досталась им нелегко, но они заслужили её.
ok: The victory did not come easily to them, but they deserved it.
bad: The victory did not come easily to them.
why: Second clause affirming they deserved it dropped.
'Рисует маслом' = paints in oils; 'draws' implies pencil/charcoal; 'by oil' is incorrect preposition.

src: Спектакль длился три часа с антрактом.
ok: The show ran for three hours including the interval.
bad: The spectacle lasted three hours with an intermission.
why: 'Спектакль' is a theatrical performance/show not a 'spectacle'; 'антракт' is an interval.

src: Он играет на гитаре уже пять лет.
ok: He has been playing the guitar for five years.
bad: He plays guitar already five years.
why: Ongoing activity requires present perfect continuous with 'for' and article before 'guitar'.

ok: The film is showing at eight in the evening.
bad: Cinema is showing at eight in the evening.
why: 'Кино' here refers to the film, not the cinema building; 'the film is showing' is correct.
'Блестяще' as an adverb means brilliantly; 'glitteringly' is not standard English.

ok: The artist created the painting in a week.
bad: The artist created a picture for a week.
why: Completed creation uses 'in a week' (duration to complete); 'for a week' implies ongoing activity.

ok: He has been passionate about chess since childhood.
bad: He is fascinated by chess from childhood.
why: Ongoing state from childhood requires present perfect; 'since childhood' not 'from childhood'.

ok: The team is in good shape.
bad: The team is in good form.
why: 'Форма' in sport context means form/shape; 'in good shape' is the more natural idiomatic English.

ok: The exhibition is open until the end of the month.
bad: The exposition is open till end of month.
why: 'Выставка' is exhibition not exposition; 'till end of month' lacks articles and is informal.

ok: The audience gave a standing ovation.
why: 'Аплодировали стоя' maps to the English idiom 'standing ovation'.
'Прослушивание' in performing arts means audition; 'hearing' is a legal/medical false friend.

ok: The stage was decorated with flowers.
bad: The scene was decorated with flowers.
why: 'Сцена' in theatre context is the stage; 'scene' is a false friend.

src: Она начала заниматься балетом в шесть лет.
ok: She started taking ballet lessons at the age of six.
bad: She began to be occupied with ballet at six years.
why: 'Заниматься балетом' means to take ballet lessons; 'at the age of six' is the correct English expression for age.

bad: He is sick for the local team.
why: 'Болеть за команду' is a Russian idiom meaning to support/root for; 'sick for' is a false literal rendering.

ok: The match ended in a draw.
why: 'Ended in a draw' requires the indefinite article; 'finished in draw' is ungrammatical.

src: Он проявил истинное мастерство в финале, и зрители были в восторге.
ok: He showed true mastery in the final, and the audience was thrilled.
bad: He showed true mastery in the final.
why: Second clause about audience reaction dropped.
Indefinite article required before 'hobby'; 'relieve stress' is the correct collocation.

src: Он играл роль злодея в этом спектакле.
ok: He played the villain in this show.
bad: He played the role of the villain in this spectacle.
why: 'Играл роль' idiomatically is 'played the villain'; 'spectacle' is a false friend for 'спектакль'.

src: Он не вылезает из тренажёрного зала.
ok: He practically lives at the gym.
bad: He doesn't climb out of the fitness hall.
why: 'Не вылезать из тренажёрного зала' idiomatically means to practically live at the gym.

src: После победы команда отпраздновала, и болельщики вышли на улицы.
ok: After the victory, the team celebrated, and the fans took to the streets.
bad: After the victory, the team celebrated.
why: Second clause about fans celebrating in the streets dropped.

ok: I need to go to the post office.
bad: To me there is needed the post.
why: Dative 'мне нужно' requires English 'I need'; 'почта' in this context means post office.

bad: To me this city is pleasing.
why: Dative 'мне нравится' requires 'I like'.

ok: I need a certificate from the clinic.
bad: To me there is needed a reference from the polyclinic.
why: Dative 'мне нужна' requires 'I need'; 'поликлиника' is clinic; 'справка' is certificate not reference.
Verb 'moves' needs adverb 'slowly', not adjective 'slow'.

ok: The document submission window is closed.
bad: Window of accepting of documents is closed.
why: Articles missing and double genitive 'of accepting of documents' is ungrammatical.

ok: The passport expired two months ago.
bad: The passport is overdue by two months.
why: 'Просрочен' for documents means expired; 'overdue' is for payments.

src: Штраф нужно оплатить до конца недели.
ok: The fine must be paid by the end of the week.
bad: The fine must be paid to the end of the week.
why: Deadline expressed with 'by', not 'to'.

ok: The application is processed within five working days.
bad: Application reviews during five working days.
why: Article missing; 'reviews' should be passive 'is processed'; 'during' should be 'within'.

bad: I respectfully request that you affix your signature to the designated location herein.
why: Routine administrative request uses polite imperative, not elaborate formal phrasing.

bad: I instruct you to obtain a numbered ticket from the dispenser!
why: Practical instruction at a service counter uses short imperative.

ok: The red tape wore him out.
why: 'Бумажная волокита' maps to 'red tape'; 'wore him out' is the natural result.

ok: The case has been dragging on for a year.
bad: The case is pulling for a year already.
why: 'Тянуться' for cases means to drag on; present perfect continuous required.

ok: The report was drawn up according to all the rules.
bad: The protocol was compiled by all the rules.
why: 'Протокол' in administrative context is an official report/record; 'protocol' is a false friend.

ok: The declaration was filed on time.
bad: The declaration was declared on time.
why: 'Подана' means filed/submitted; 'declared' is a circular false calque.

src: Квитанция выдана кассиром и подтверждает оплату.
ok: The receipt was issued by the cashier and confirms the payment.
bad: The receipt was issued by the cashier.
why: Second clause confirming payment dropped.

src: Несмотря на очередь, он получил документы в тот же день.
ok: Despite the queue, he received the documents the same day.
bad: He received the documents the same day.
why: Concessive clause 'несмотря на очередь' dropped.

src: Прием граждан ведётся по предварительной записи.
bad: Receiving of citizens is conducted by preliminary record.
why: 'По предварительной записи' = by appointment; 'by preliminary record' is a false calque.

src: Ему нужно поставить штамп в паспорт.
ok: He needs to have his passport stamped.
bad: To him there is needed to put a stamp into the passport.
why: Dative 'ему нужно' requires 'he needs'; causative 'have his passport stamped' required.
Transport 'runs' not 'goes'; 'on schedule' not 'by schedule'.

ok: There is a lot of traffic in the city centre.
bad: In the city centre there are many traffic jams.
why: 'Много пробок' can be rendered as 'a lot of traffic'; 'many traffic jams' is also correct but less natural.

ok: The playground is closed for renovation.
bad: The children's playground is closed on repair.
why: 'Closed for renovation' requires 'for', not 'on'; the modifier is redundant.

ok: The municipality is responsible for street cleanliness.
bad: The municipality is responsible for cleanliness of streets.
why: Compound noun 'street cleanliness' is more natural than genitive 'cleanliness of streets'.

ok: He lives in a residential area.
bad: He lives in a sleeping district.
why: 'Спальный район' means residential/suburban area; 'sleeping district' is a false literal.

bad: The signboard on the shop is obsolete.
why: 'Устарела' for a sign means outdated; 'obsolete' implies no longer functioning.

src: Светофор не работает на этом перекрёстке.
ok: The traffic light is out of order at this intersection.
bad: The traffic light does not work on this crossroads.
why: 'Out of order' is the natural English idiom for broken equipment; 'crossroads' is British English; 'intersection' is more standard.

src: Парковка запрещена с семи до девяти утра.
ok: Parking is prohibited from seven to nine in the morning.
bad: Parking is forbidden from seven till nine in the morning.
why: 'Prohibited' is the standard term for traffic/civic regulations; 'from...to' is preferred over 'from...till' in formal notices.

src: Он снял квартиру недалеко от метро.
ok: He rented a flat near the metro.
bad: He removed an apartment not far from the subway.
why: 'Снял квартиру' means rented a flat; 'removed' is a false calque; 'метро' can be metro.
'Стоит остро' means is pressing/acute; 'stands sharply' is a false literal calque.

bad: The debt on communal services grows.
why: 'Коммуналка' = utilities; 'communal services' is a literal calque; present progressive preferred for ongoing growth.

src: Дорога строилась два года, и в итоге её открыли досрочно.

bad: The road was under construction for two years.
why: Second clause about early opening dropped.

src: Он обратился в горсовет с жалобой.

bad: He addressed himself to the city council with a complaint.
why: 'Обратился с жалобой' = filed a complaint; 'addressed himself to' is non-standard.

bad: The route of bus was changed.
why: 'Bus route' is a compound noun; 'route of bus' lacks article and uses wrong structure.

src: Контролёр проверил билеты у всех пассажиров.

bad: The controller checked tickets at all passengers.

src: Нарушитель заплатил штраф и был предупреждён повторно.
ok: The violator paid the fine and was warned again.
why: Second clause about the warning dropped.

ok: Utility bills go up every year.
bad: Communal services become more expensive every year.
why: 'Дорожать' for bills means go up; 'utility bills' is the natural English term.

ok: The lift is out of order. Please use the stairs.
bad: The elevator is broken. Use the staircase.
why: 'Out of order' is the standard notice; 'Please use' is more polite in public signage.

src: Посетитель написал жалобу в книгу отзывов.
ok: The visitor wrote a complaint in the feedback book.
bad: The visitor wrote a complaint in the book of reviews.

src: Пешеходная зона введена в прошлом году.

bad: Pedestrian zone was entered in last year.

src: Он нашёл работу через центр занятости.

bad: He found work through the centre of employment.
why: 'Работу' in job context is 'a job'; 'employment centre' is the standard compound noun.

src: В нашем городе хороший общественный транспорт.

bad: In our city there is good public transport.
why: 'Our city has' is more natural for general description; both are acceptable but 'has' is preferred.

bad: The street illumination went out of order.
why: 'Освещение' is lighting not illumination; 'broke down' is more natural than 'went out of order'.

src: Мэр открыл новый парк в центре города.

bad: The mayor has opened new park in the centre of city.
why: Simple past for completed one-time event; articles required; 'city centre' as compound noun.

src: Доступ в здание ограничен для посторонних.

Full building work is renovation; 'repaired' implies fixing specific damage.

src: Новый торговый центр открылся на прошлой неделе, и уже полон посетителей.
ok: The new shopping centre opened last week and is already full of visitors.
bad: The new shopping centre opened last week.
why: Second clause about being full of visitors dropped.

bad: To me it is pleasing to plan budget.

bad: At him there are no savings.
why: 'У него нет' requires English subject-verb 'he has no'.

bad: Prices on real estate growed over two years.
why: 'Property prices' is the natural compound; 'growed' is non-standard past participle — 'risen' required.

ok: The loan was approved three days ago.

why: Specific past time 'ago' requires simple past, not present perfect.

ok: The bank charges a fee for transfers.
bad: Bank collects a commission for transfers.

bad: Debt grows because of high percents.

why: Common warning uses direct imperative, not elaborate formal phrasing.
Russian proverb about financial diligence requires a natural English paraphrase.
Plural subject 'pockets' requires plural verb 'are'.

src: Не складывай все яйца в одну корзину.

bad: Do not fold all eggs into one basket.
why: Russian idiom has an exact English equivalent.

bad: Inflation grows third year in a row.
why: Present perfect continuous required for ongoing trend; 'in a row' or 'running' preferred.
'Акционер' = shareholder/stockholder; 'actioner' is a false friend.
'Курс' in financial context is exchange rate not course.

src: Он вложил деньги в акции, и они принесли хорошую прибыль.
ok: He invested in stocks, and they generated a good profit.
why: Second clause about profit generated dropped.

src: Несмотря на кризис, компания осталась прибыльной.
ok: Despite the crisis, the company remained profitable.
why: Concessive clause 'несмотря на кризис' dropped.

src: Страховой полис покрывает ущерб от пожара.
ok: The insurance policy covers damage from fire.
bad: The insurance police covers damage from fire.
why: 'Полис' = insurance policy; 'police' is a false friend.

ok: The mortgage is paid off over twenty years.
why: 'Выплачивается' = is paid off; 'over twenty years' is the correct preposition; 'pays' is active.

ok: The account has been frozen pending an investigation.
bad: The account is frozen until clarification of circumstances.
why: Present perfect passive for recently-enacted state; 'pending an investigation' is the natural phrase.

ok: The family budget is bursting at the seams.
bad: The family budget crackles at its seams.
why: 'Трещит по швам' maps to English idiom 'bursting at the seams'.

src: Он взял кредит под низкий процент.

bad: He took a credit under a low percent.
why: 'Взял кредит' = took out a loan; 'under' should be 'at'; 'percent' should be 'interest rate'.

src: Налоги в этой стране очень высокие.

'Экономит' in context of spending means saves money; 'on all' should be 'on everything'.

src: Рост акций обусловлен хорошим квартальным отчётом.

ok: It is time to tighten our belts.
bad: It is time to pull the waistband.
why: 'Затянуть пояс' maps to English idiom 'tighten our belts'.

src: Пенсия выплачивается первого числа каждого месяца.
ok: The pension is paid on the first of each month.
bad: Pension is paid at first number of each month.
why: Article missing; 'первого числа' = on the first; 'at first number' is a false literal calque.

ok: The transfer arrived in the account yesterday.
bad: The translation arrived into the account yesterday.
why: 'Перевод' in banking context is a transfer; 'translation' is the false friend.

src: Он потратил всё состояние на бизнес, но вернул вложения с прибылью.
ok: He spent his entire fortune on the business, but recovered the investment with profit.
bad: He spent his entire fortune on the business.
why: Second clause about recovering the investment dropped.

src: Несмотря на инфляцию, он не снижал уровень жизни.
ok: Despite inflation, he did not lower his standard of living.
bad: He did not lower his standard of living.
why: Concessive clause 'несмотря на инфляцию' dropped.

src: Зарплата у него хорошая, но расходы ещё больше.

bad: His salary is good but expenses more.
why: Comparison requires 'even higher'; 'expenses more' is ungrammatical.

ok: He went bankrupt due to a bad investment.
bad: He bankrupted due to unsuccessful investment.
why: 'Обанкротился' = went bankrupt; 'bankrupted' is not standard intransitive.

ok: The country's economy is recovering from the crisis.
bad: Economy of the country is restoring after crisis.
why: 'Восстанавливается' = is recovering; 'restoring' implies an agent; articles missing.
'Стала редкостью' = has become a rarity; 'became seldom' uses an adjective where a noun is needed.

ok: Money is not the most important thing in life.
bad: Money is not the main in life.
why: 'Главное' requires the full adjective phrase 'most important thing'; 'the main' is elliptical and non-standard.
'Играть на бирже' idiomatically means to play the stock market.

ok: The loan is repaid in instalments.
why: 'Возвращается' for a loan is 'repaid'; 'in instalments' is the financial collocation.

ok: The budget has been approved for the next year.
bad: Budget is affirmed for next year.
why: 'Утверждён' = has been approved; 'affirmed' is non-standard; articles missing.

src: Она работает в банке уже десять лет.
ok: She has been working at the bank for ten years.
bad: She works in bank already ten years.
why: Ongoing action requires present perfect continuous with 'for'; article missing.

src: Экономить нужно с умом, тогда деньги будут всегда.
ok: Save money wisely, and you will always have it.
bad: You need to economise with mind.
why: Second clause about always having money dropped; phrasing also weak.

src: Расходы превысили доходы в этом квартале.

why: 'Превысили' = exceeded; 'доходы' = income (singular) not revenues; article not needed.

ok: The card has been blocked due to suspicious transactions.
bad: The card is blocked because of suspicious operations.
why: Present perfect passive for recently-enacted state; 'transactions' is the standard banking term over 'operations'.

src: Не берите кредит, если не уверены в доходах.
ok: Don't take out a loan if you are not sure about your income.
bad: Do not take credit if you are not sure about revenues.
why: 'Кредит' = loan (take out a loan); 'доходах' = income not revenues.

src: Её зарплата увеличилась вдвое за год.

bad: Her wage increased twofold during a year.
why: 'Зарплата' = salary; 'увеличилась вдвое' = doubled; 'in a year' not 'during a year'.

ok: He sticks to a strict budget.
bad: He adheres to a strict budget.
why: 'Придерживается' colloquially = sticks to; 'adheres to' is more formal than the source.

ok: He is as rich as Croesus.

'Jealouses' is not a verb; 'envies' is the correct verb for 'завидует'.

why: Encouragement uses short imperative, not formal phrasing.
