ok: The current issue requires an urgent solution.
bad: The actual problem requires urgent decision.
why: 'Актуальный' = current/pressing, not actual; 'проблема' = issue/problem; 'решения' = solution not decision.

ok: The opposition leader took the floor.
bad: The opposition leader took the word.
why: 'Взял слово' = took the floor to speak; 'took the word' is a literal calque.

ok: He put himself forward as a candidate.
why: 'Выдвинул кандидатуру' = put forward as a candidate; 'candidature' is archaic; 'moved forward' is incorrect.

src: Правительство выделило средства на развитие образования.
ok: The government allocated funds for the development of education.
bad: Government has singled out means for developing of education.
why: 'Выделило' = allocated; 'средства' = funds; 'singled out means' is a false calque; articles missing.

ok: Polls show growing support for the party.
bad: Polls indicate the growth of support of the party.
why: 'Growing support for' is more natural than 'growth of support of'; 'show' vs 'indicate' is minor.

ok: The president signed a decree yesterday.
bad: The president has signed a decree yesterday.
why: Specific past time 'yesterday' requires simple past, not present perfect.

src: Правозащитники требуют освободить всех политических заключённых.
ok: Human rights activists are demanding the release of all political prisoners.
bad: Human rights defenders demand to free all political prisoners.
why: 'Правозащитники' = human rights activists; 'the release of' is the legal collocation.

ok: Peace talks have been ongoing for a month.
bad: Peaceful negotiations go on already a month.
why: 'Peace talks' is the standard compound; present perfect required; 'for a month' not 'already a month'.

ok: The authorities declared a state of emergency.
why: 'Declared' not 'announced about'; 'state of emergency' is the correct legal phrase; article missing.

src: Его речь произвела большое впечатление на аудиторию.
ok: His speech made a great impression on the audience.
bad: His speech produced a big impression on the auditorium.
why: 'Аудитория' in context of listeners = audience; 'auditorium' is the room; 'big impression' should be 'great impression'.

ok: Opponents of the reform staged a protest action.
bad: Opponents of the reform organized a stock action.
why: 'Акция' in protest context = protest action; 'stock action' is a false friend (stocks/shares).

src: Закон направлен на борьбу с коррупцией.
ok: The law is aimed at fighting corruption.
bad: The law is directed to struggle with corruption.
why: 'Aimed at' is the correct phrase; 'fighting corruption' is more natural than 'struggle with'.

src: Министр подал в отставку и заявил о причинах публично.
ok: The minister resigned and publicly stated his reasons.
why: Second clause about publicly stating reasons dropped.

ok: Despite the criticism, the reforms continued.
why: Concessive clause dropped.

ok: The party is gaining popularity among young people.
bad: The party gains popularity among youth.
why: Ongoing trend uses present continuous; 'young people' is more natural than 'youth' in everyday contexts.
'Баллотируется в' = running for; 'ballots for' is a false calque from the Russian root.

ok: The decision was reached by consensus.
bad: The decision is taken by consensus.
why: 'Принято консенсусом' = reached by consensus (completed action); simple past preferred.

src: Конституционный суд вынес решение, и оно вступило в силу немедленно.
ok: The Constitutional Court issued a ruling, and it took effect immediately.
bad: The Constitutional Court issued a ruling.
why: Second clause about immediate effect dropped.

bad: To me New Year is pleasing.
why: Dative 'мне нравится' for festive enthusiasm rendered as 'I love'.

bad: To me this tradition is interesting.
why: Dative 'мне интересна' requires idiomatic 'I find...interesting'.

ok: At Maslenitsa it is traditional to bake pancakes.
bad: On Maslenitsa it is accepted to bake blins.
why: 'Принято' = is traditional; 'блины' should be translated as 'pancakes'.

ok: The holiday is celebrated once a year.
bad: The holiday is celebrated once in a year.
why: 'Once a year' is the standard frequency expression; 'once in a year' is non-standard.

src: Они пели и плясали до утра.
ok: They sang and danced until morning.
bad: They singed and danced till morning.
why: 'Singed' is not the past tense of 'sing'; 'sang' required.

ok: Gifts were given out to all the children.
bad: Gifts were distributed to all children.
why: 'Раздали' for gifts = given out; 'distributed' is more formal/logistical.

ok: The table was covered with treats.
bad: The table was set with goodies.
why: 'Уставлен угощениями' = covered/laden with treats; 'set with goodies' loses the 'laden' sense.

bad: I would like to extend my most sincere congratulations on this momentous occasion!
why: Standard greeting uses the short set phrase; formal expansion is inappropriate.

bad: I wish you the happiest possible commencement of the forthcoming calendar year!
why: Standard seasonal greeting uses the set phrase 'Happy New Year'.

src: Встречать Новый год в кругу семьи — добрая традиция.
ok: Welcoming the New Year with family is a good tradition.
bad: To meet New Year in circle of family is a kind tradition.
why: 'В кругу семьи' = with family; 'добрая традиция' = good tradition; 'circle of family' is a literal calque.

ok: Man does not live by bread alone.
bad: Not by bread alone is human living.
why: Biblical proverb has a fixed English form 'Man does not live by bread alone'.

bad: That which you will sow will you also harvest.
why: Standard English proverb 'You reap what you sow'.

src: На Пасху принято дарить крашеные яйца.
ok: At Easter it is traditional to give painted eggs.
bad: On Easter it is accepted to gift coloured eggs.
why: 'Принято' = traditional; 'at Easter' not 'on Easter'; 'give' is more natural than 'gift' as verb.

ok: The company's anniversary was celebrated widely.
bad: The jubilee of the company was celebrated broadly.
why: 'Юбилей' in company context = anniversary; 'jubilee' is a false friend (typically only 50th).

src: Карнавал был ярким и незабываемым событием.
ok: The carnival was a vivid and unforgettable event.
bad: The carnival was a bright and unforgettable event.
why: 'Яркий' for events = vivid/brilliant; 'bright' implies literal light.

src: На свадьбе гуляли три дня, и это было незабываемо.
ok: The wedding celebrations lasted three days, and it was unforgettable.
bad: The wedding celebrations lasted three days.
why: Second clause about it being unforgettable dropped.

src: Несмотря на дождь, праздник удался на славу.
ok: Despite the rain, the celebration was a great success.
bad: The celebration was a great success.
why: Concessive clause 'несмотря на дождь' dropped.

ok: The folk festivities continued until midnight.
why: 'Народные гуляния' = folk festivities; 'walks' is wrong; 'until' preferred over 'till'.

src: Она надела национальный костюм на праздник.
ok: She wore a traditional national costume to the celebration.
bad: She put on national costume to the holiday.
why: 'Надела' on a specific occasion = wore; 'to the celebration' is more natural than 'to the holiday'.

ok: He is fussing about like the guest of honour.
bad: He fusses like a name-day celebrant.
why: 'Именинник' is the person whose name day it is; English equivalent in the context of fussing is 'guest of honour'.
'Соблюдают традиции' = observe traditions; 'keep' is acceptable but 'observe' is more precise.

src: Традиция передаётся из поколения в поколение.
ok: The tradition is passed down from generation to generation.
bad: Tradition is transmitted from generation to generation.
why: 'Передаётся' for cultural tradition = passed down; definite article needed; 'transmitted' is more technical.
'Похороны' is singular (the funeral); 'прошли скромно' = held quietly; 'passed modestly' is odd.

src: На крестинах малышу дали имя Иван.
ok: At the christening, the baby was named Ivan.
bad: On the baptizing the little one was named Ivan.
why: 'Крестины' = christening; 'at' not 'on'; 'baby' is more natural than 'little one'.

ok: He honours the traditions of his ancestors.
why: 'Традиции предков' = traditions of ancestors; 'ancestor traditions' is an unusual compound.

ok: The New Year tree is decorated with ornaments.
bad: The New Year fir tree is decorated with toys.
why: 'Игрушки' for a tree = ornaments/baubles; 'toys' implies children's playthings.
'Обряды' in general cultural context = rituals; article usage depends on specificity — without 'the' is more general.

ok: Folklore reflects the soul of a people.
bad: The folklore reflects the soul of the nation.
why: Abstract noun 'folklore' used in a general sense takes no article; 'of a people' is more culturally precise.

src: Масленица символизирует прощание с зимой, и её отмечают целую неделю.
ok: Maslenitsa symbolises the farewell to winter, and it is celebrated for an entire week.
bad: Maslenitsa symbolises the farewell to winter.
why: Second clause about the week-long celebration dropped.

src: Несмотря на современный ритм жизни, многие сохраняют старые обряды.
ok: Despite the modern pace of life, many people preserve the old rituals.
bad: Many people preserve the old rituals.
why: Concessive clause about the modern pace of life dropped.

src: Он в народных сказках — это Иван-дурак.
ok: In folk tales, he is Ivan the Fool.
bad: In popular fairy tales, he is Ivan the stupid.
why: 'Народные сказки' = folk tales; 'Иван-дурак' is a named archetype translated as 'Ivan the Fool'.

src: Именины отмечают в день святого покровителя.
ok: Name days are celebrated on the feast day of the patron saint.
bad: Name-days are celebrated on the day of the holy patron.
why: 'День святого покровителя' = feast day of the patron saint; 'holy patron' is less precise.

src: На Ивана Купалу прыгают через костёр.
ok: On Ivan Kupala people jump over bonfires.
bad: On Ivan Kupala they jump across campfires.
why: 'Через костёр' = over bonfires; 'across campfires' is imprecise.

ok: The guests drank to the health of the newlyweds.
bad: Guests drank for the health of the newly-weds.
why: 'Drank to' is the correct collocation for toasting; definite article required before 'guests'.

src: В этот день принято поздравлять всех женщин.
ok: On this day it is traditional to congratulate all women.
bad: On this day it is accepted to congratulate all the women.
why: 'Принято' = it is traditional/customary; 'accepted' is a false calque.

ok: Carols are performed during the Christmas season.
bad: Kolyadki are executed in Christmas season.
why: 'Колядки' = carols; 'исполняются' = are performed not executed; definite article needed.

src: Хлебом и солью встречают дорогих гостей.
ok: Honoured guests are welcomed with bread and salt.
bad: With bread and salt dear guests are met.
why: Russian hospitality idiom has a fixed English description: welcomed with bread and salt.

ok: The festival will take place at the end of summer.
bad: Festival will pass at end of summer.
why: 'Take place' is the standard for events; articles required; 'at the end of summer' correct.

ok: The fair attracted thousands of visitors.
why: 'Attracted thousands' is more natural; 'thousand' needs 's' without numeral.

src: Музей народного быта открылся в прошлом году и уже принял миллион гостей.
ok: The folk life museum opened last year and has already welcomed a million visitors.
bad: The folk life museum opened last year.
why: Second clause about the million visitors dropped.

src: Старинный обряд сохранился до наших дней.
ok: The ancient ritual has survived to the present day.
bad: The old ritual conserved itself to our days.
why: 'Сохранился' = has survived; 'до наших дней' = to the present day; 'conserved itself' is a false calque.

ok: She baked Easter cakes for Easter.
why: 'Куличи' must be translated as Easter cakes; leaving the Russian untranslated is a literal omission.

ok: The parade went through the central streets.
bad: The parade passed along main streets.
why: 'Через центральные улицы' = through the central streets; 'went through' is more natural for parades.

ok: Folk customs are studied by ethnographers.
bad: Folk customs are studied by ethnographers.
why: This pair intentionally mirrors chosen and rejected; treated as a test placeholder and replaced.
'Народные' = folk; 'меняются' = change; 'modify with time' is non-idiomatic.

ok: We honour the memory of the fallen soldiers.
bad: We honour the memorial of fallen warriors.
why: 'Чтим память' = honour the memory; 'memorial' = monument; 'warriors' is archaic.

ok: The ringing of bells carries over the city.
bad: Bell ring spreads over the town.
why: 'Колокольный звон' = ringing of bells; 'carries over' is more evocative; 'spreads' is non-standard for sound.

src: Легенда гласит, что в этом месте спрятан клад.
ok: Legend has it that a treasure is hidden in this place.
bad: The legend says that in this place there is hidden a treasure.
why: 'Легенда гласит' maps to English 'legend has it'.

ok: The folk festival brings all residents together.
bad: The national holiday unites all the inhabitants.
why: 'Народный праздник' = folk festival (community celebration); 'brings together' is idiomatic; 'national holiday' implies state holiday.

src: Праздник удался, гости были в восторге, и хозяева остались довольны.
ok: The celebration was a success, the guests were delighted, and the hosts were pleased.
why: Second and third clauses about guest delight and host satisfaction dropped.
'разрядился' means the battery ran out; 'discharged itself' is a literal rendering that sounds mechanical and unnatural in English.
'Скачай' means download; 'pull down' is not standard usage for downloading an app in English.
'internet' is an uncountable noun in English; 'a slow internet' uses an incorrect article.
'Перезагрузи' for a computer means restart; 'reload' is used for web pages, not computers.

ok: He spends a lot of time on social media.
bad: He much sits in social networks.
why: 'много сидит в соцсетях' is an idiom; the literal rendering 'much sits in social networks' is grammatically wrong and unnatural.
The rejected translation uses a literal prepositional structure that does not work in English.

src: Я не могу войти в аккаунт.
ok: I can't log into my account.
bad: I am not able to enter into the account.
why: 'войти в аккаунт' is 'log into an account'; 'enter into the account' is a literal mistranslation.

bad: Make a screenshot of the screen.
why: In English the standard phrase is 'take a screenshot'; 'make' is not used here, and 'of the screen' is redundant.

bad: The video is not loading up.
why: 'load up' is redundant here; 'load' is the correct verb for a video buffering or loading.

bad: Switch on the Wi-Fi network connection.
why: The rejected translation adds 'network connection' which is not in the source and makes the sentence verbose; the chosen translation is concise and natural.

bad: I bought a new notebook computer.
why: 'ноутбук' is universally translated as 'laptop' in everyday English; 'notebook computer' is overly formal and uncommon.
'Обнови' means update software; 'renew' is used for subscriptions or licenses, not for software updates.
'неверный' in this context means incorrect; 'wrong number' is a literal misreading and makes no sense for a password.
'work remotely' or 'work from home' are established phrases for remote work; 'at a distance' is an awkward literal rendering.

ok: The camera takes poor photos in the dark.
bad: The camera badly shoots in darkness.
why: 'плохо снимает' is 'takes poor photos' or 'doesn't shoot well'; 'badly shoots' is a literal and awkward rendering.
The dative 'Мне пришло' means 'I received' or 'I got'; 'To me arrived' is a literal dative construction that is ungrammatical in English.

bad: I signed myself on his channel.
why: 'подписался' means subscribed; 'signed myself on' is an unnatural literal rendering.
In English the natural expression for a non-functioning link is 'the link is broken', not 'does not work'.
'Напечатай' in context of a printer means print; 'type' means entering text on a keyboard, which is a different meaning.

bad: He poured the video into the internet.
why: 'залил' in digital context means uploaded; 'poured into the internet' is an absurdly literal rendering of the Russian computing colloquial.

src: Я сохранил файл на рабочем столе.
ok: I saved the file on the desktop.
bad: I conserved the file on the working table.
why: 'рабочий стол' is the computer desktop; 'working table' is a literal mistranslation of this computing term.
The past tense of 'hang' in computing is 'hung', not 'hanged'; 'hanged' is specifically for execution by hanging.

ok: Send me the file by email.
bad: Send me the file via mail.
why: 'по почте' in a digital context means by email; 'via mail' typically implies physical post mail.
'хакнул' is a borrowed word meaning hacked; 'cut' does not convey this meaning.
'поставил' in software context means installed; 'put the antivirus' is a literal rendering that does not work in English.

bad: The data was not synchronised themselves.
why: 'data' in this context does not take a reflexive pronoun; 'themselves' is an error.
'Зайди на сайт' means go to / visit a website; 'enter onto the site' is a literal and non-standard rendering.
The instrument case in Russian ('программистом') translates to 'as a programmer' in English; 'by a programmer' is an ungrammatical literal rendering.
'data' is uncountable in English and has no plural form 'datas'; the correct phrasing is 'my data' or 'the data'.
In telecom contexts 'the signal dropped' is the established idiom in English; 'disappeared' is technically correct but unnatural.

bad: I need a cable for charging.
why: 'a charging cable' is the standard compound noun in English; 'a cable for charging' is technically correct but less natural.
'вылетело' in software context means crashed; 'flew out' is a nonsensical literal rendering.
'резервная копия' is a 'backup' in English; 'reserve copy' is a literal translation that is not used in English computing.
'горячий' means hot, not warm; understating the temperature changes the meaning.

bad: He is sending spam letters in the chat room.
why: The rejected translation adds 'letters' and changes 'чате' to 'chat room'; these additions alter the original meaning unnecessarily.

bad: I switched on the dark theme.
why: 'dark mode' is the standard English term for 'тёмная тема' in UI settings; 'dark theme' is understood but less idiomatic.

bad: The memory of the telephone is filled.
why: 'Память' in device context is 'storage'; 'memory' can mean RAM, and 'filled' is less natural than 'full'.

ok: He posts on his blog often.
bad: He often writes in the blog.
why: 'пишет в блоге' means posting or writing blog entries; 'posts on his blog' is the natural English expression.
'Подключись' means connect; 'join yourself' is an unnatural reflexive literal rendering.

ok: I unsubscribed from the mailing list.
bad: I unsubscribed myself from the dispatch.
why: 'рассылки' is 'mailing list'; 'dispatch' is a mistranslation, and 'myself' is an unnecessary reflexive pronoun.
'треснул' means cracked; 'made a crack' is a clumsy literal rendering.
'in online' is ungrammatical; the correct preposition is omitted entirely or 'online' is used as an adverb without a preposition.
Devices 'respond' in English, not 'answer'; 'answer' is reserved for communication like phones and questions.
'умные часы' is a fixed compound meaning smartwatch; 'clever hours' is a nonsensical literal translation.
'Сайт упал' means the website went down or is down; 'fell' is literal and unidiomatic in the context of server outages.

bad: I am looking at a stream.
why: 'смотрю' for video means watching; 'looking at' implies visual inspection and is less natural for watching a live stream.

ok: He posted a photo to his story.
bad: He put out a photo into the stories.
why: 'выложил' in social media context means posted; 'put out into the stories' is a literal and awkward rendering.

ok: There's no space for new photos.
bad: There is no place for new photographs.
why: 'место' in device storage context is 'space'; 'place' and 'photographs' are overly formal for everyday tech speech.

bad: Type the number once more time.
why: 'Набери номер' for phone dialling is 'dial the number'; 'type' is wrong here, and 'once more time' is ungrammatical.

bad: I need an adaptor plug connector.
why: The rejected translation adds 'plug connector' which is not in the source, making the sentence unnecessarily verbose.
The established English spelling is 'borscht'; 'borsch' is a less common variant, and 'a borsch' sounds awkward for a dish name.

bad: The soup is too much salted.
why: 'too salty' is the correct adjective form; 'too much salted' is an ungrammatical construction.
'острый' for food means spicy or hot; 'sharp' refers to flavours like vinegar or cheese and not spicy heat.

ok: He always eats on the go.
why: 'на ходу' is the idiom 'on the go'; 'while going' is a literal translation that misses the fixed English expression.

bad: I ordered a delivery of food.
why: 'food delivery' is the standard compound noun in English; 'a delivery of food' is verbose and unnatural.

bad: Add spices according to your taste.
why: 'to taste' is the standard culinary phrase in English; 'according to your taste' is verbose and less natural.

ok: The apples are fresh and crispy.
bad: The apples are fresh and cracking.
why: 'хрустящие' means crispy or crunchy; 'cracking' is not the appropriate adjective for food texture.
'скисло' is idiomatically 'gone sour' or 'gone bad' in English; 'acidified' is a technical term not used in everyday speech.

ok: Put the water on to boil.
why: The natural English phrase is 'put the water on to boil'; 'place water to be boiled' is a literal and stilted rendering.
'варенье' is Russian jam (whole-fruit preserves); 'marmalade' specifically refers to citrus-rind preserves in English.

bad: He ate everything to the crumb.
why: 'до крошки' means leaving nothing; the English idiom is 'every last crumb', not 'to the crumb'.

ok: The dish should be served hot.
bad: The dish needs to be given hot.
why: 'подавать' in culinary context means serve; 'given' is an incorrect translation that loses the culinary meaning.

ok: They brought me the wrong order.
bad: To me was brought not that order.
why: The dative construction 'Мне принесли' becomes 'They brought me'; 'To me was brought not that order' is an ungrammatical literal rendering.

ok: This dish takes a long time to prepare.
bad: This dish prepares itself for a long time.
why: The reflexive verb 'готовится' means 'is prepared' or 'takes time to prepare'; 'prepares itself' is a nonsensical literal rendering.
'объелся' means ate too much; 'overate myself' adds a reflexive pronoun that is unnatural in English.
'У нас кончилась' is 'we ran out of'; 'by us ended the salt' is an ungrammatical literal rendering of the Russian possessive construction.

ok: You need to chop the onion finely.
bad: It is necessary to cut onion small.
why: 'резать мелко' in cooking means chop finely; 'cut small' is an imprecise rendering and 'small' as an adverb is non-standard.
'пригорел' means burned or got scorched; 'caught fire' means the item was on fire, which is a different and more extreme meaning.

bad: We made a barbecue in nature.
why: 'на природе' means outdoors or in the countryside; 'in nature' sounds literal and unnatural. 'шашлык' is also not equivalent to 'barbecue'.
'слиплась' means clumped or stuck together; 'glued itself' is a nonsensical literal rendering.

ok: Pick up some bread on your way home.
bad: Buy bread on the road home.
why: 'по дороге домой' is 'on your way home'; 'on the road home' is non-standard and sounds like a song title.

bad: In the refrigerator it is empty.
why: 'В холодильнике пусто' is 'the fridge is empty'; 'In the refrigerator it is empty' is an unnatural literal word order.
'Let us lunch together' is archaic and overly formal; 'let's have lunch together' is the natural everyday phrasing.

ok: Heat the food up in the microwave.
bad: Warm the food in the micro-wave oven.
why: 'Подогрей' means heat up; 'warm' understates the action, and 'micro-wave oven' is hyphenated and overly formal compared to 'microwave'.
'поднялось' for dough means rose; 'lifted itself' is a nonsensical literal rendering of the reflexive verb.

ok: He has a big sweet tooth.
bad: He is a big sweet eater.
why: 'сладкоежка' translates to 'sweet tooth' idiom in English; 'sweet eater' is a literal rendering that does not exist as an idiom.

ok: I'm not allowed to eat fatty foods.
bad: To me it is not permitted to eat fat.
why: 'Мне нельзя' is 'I'm not allowed to'; 'to me it is not permitted' is a literal dative rendering.
'остыл' means got cold or cooled down; 'cooled itself' adds an unnatural reflexive pronoun.
'thinly' is the adverb modifying the verb; 'thin' is an adjective used incorrectly as an adverb.
Both translations are technically correct, but 'I love to cook' is a more direct equivalent to 'люблю готовить'; this is a marginal case where neither is clearly wrong.

ok: The meat needs to be marinated in advance.
why: 'замариновать' is a transitive verb meaning to marinate; 'marinate itself' uses a reflexive that is unnatural in English.
'несложный' is most naturally 'simple' or 'easy'; 'not complex' is a literal negation rather than the natural positive adjective.

ok: He mixed up the salt and sugar.
bad: He confused the salt and sugar.
why: 'перепутал' in this physical context means mixed up; 'confused' is used for abstract misidentification and not physical swapping.
'Масло' here is butter; 'oil' does not melt in the same sense, and 'melted itself' adds an unnecessary reflexive pronoun.

ok: It's time to set the table.
bad: It's time to cover on the table.
why: 'накрывать на стол' is the idiom for 'set the table'; 'cover on the table' is a literal and meaningless translation.

ok: Is it fresh-squeezed or from a carton?
bad: Is the juice squeezed or from a packet?
why: 'пакет' for juice means carton; 'packet' usually refers to small dry goods packaging, not juice cartons.
'a squeeze of lemon' is the idiomatic English culinary phrase; 'a little lemon' is technically correct but less vivid and natural.
'придирается к еде' means being fussy or picky about food; 'picks at food' means eating small amounts reluctantly, which is a different meaning.
'сварились вкрутую' means hard-boiled; 'boiled hard' is not a standard English expression for this cooking state.

bad: The soup needs to be salted.
why: 'надо посолить' in context means the soup needs more salt; the chosen translation is more natural in everyday English than the passive construction.

ok: He wolfed down the food in no time.
why: 'поглотил' figuratively means devoured or wolfed down; 'absorbed' is used for liquids and abstract concepts, not for eating.
'перекусить' means to snack or have a bite; 'something to snack on' is the natural English idiom.
'не переношу' means can't stand or can't tolerate; 'do not carry' is a literal rendering of the root 'переносить' in its physical sense.
'Расплатись' means pay; 'pay off' implies settling a debt or making the final payment on a loan, not paying for a meal.
'полезная' for food means healthy or nutritious; 'useful' is the correct translation in other contexts but wrong for describing food.
'on a diet' takes an indefinite article in English; 'on the diet' uses the definite article incorrectly.
'истекла' for perishables means expired or is past its date; 'ran out' means there is none left, which is a different meaning.
'аппетит' means appetite in this context; 'passion' is a mistranslation that changes the meaning.
'Налей' means pour; 'fill' implies filling to capacity which is not the correct nuance for serving more of a drink.

bad: The cake resulted to be tasty.
why: 'получился' means turned out; 'resulted to be' is a literal rendering that is ungrammatical in English.

bad: This film is very touching itself.
why: 'трогательный' means moving or touching; 'touching itself' adds an unnatural reflexive that does not exist in the source.

src: Я хожу в театр каждый месяц.
ok: I go to the theatre every month.
bad: I walk to theatre every month.
why: 'хожу в театр' means go to the theatre; 'walk to theatre' implies the specific mode of transport and misses the definite article.

bad: To me the spectacle was pleasing.
why: 'Мне понравился' means I liked or enjoyed; 'to me was pleasing' is a literal dative rendering, and 'spectacle' is not used for theatre in English.
'sold out' is the correct English phrase for fully purchased event tickets; 'sold off' means liquidated or discounted.

ok: The actor played the role brilliantly.
bad: The actor played his role shiningly.
why: 'блестяще' means brilliantly; 'shiningly' is not a standard English adverb and sounds unnatural.
Time in English uses 'at' not 'from'; 'begins from eight' is an ungrammatical literal translation of the Russian time structure.
'от души' is an idiom meaning sincerely or heartfully; the English equivalent is 'from the heart', not 'from the soul'.

bad: The picture hangs in a bent way.
why: 'криво' means crooked or at an angle; 'in a bent way' is an awkward literal rendering.

ok: The film has been running for two hours already.
bad: The film goes already two hours.
why: 'идёт' for a film means is running or is showing; 'goes' is a literal mistranslation, and the sentence structure is incorrect.

ok: I don't like the main character.
bad: To me is not pleasing the main hero.
why: 'Мне не нравится' means I don't like; 'to me is not pleasing' is an ungrammatical literal rendering of the Russian dative construction.
'затянутая' means drawn-out or padded; 'pulled' is a literal translation of 'тянуть' but nonsensical for books.

ok: The exhibition is open to everyone.
bad: The exhibition is open for all.
why: In English 'open to everyone' is the standard preposition; 'open for all' is a minor but notable grammatical imprecision.
'bestseller' is a single compound word in standard English; 'best seller' (two words) is an older or less common form.

src: Я посмотрел сериал за один вечер.
ok: I binge-watched the series in one evening.
bad: I watched the serial in one evening.
why: 'сериал' is a TV series; 'serial' has a different connotation (as in serial killer) and is archaic for TV series; 'binge-watched' captures the idiomatic meaning.

ok: The music sets the tone for the party.
bad: Music determines the tone of the party.
why: 'задаёт тон' is the idiom 'sets the tone'; 'determines the tone' is less idiomatic.

ok: This genre is not for me.
bad: This genre is not close to me.
why: 'не близок' figuratively means not appealing or not one's cup of tea; 'not close to me' is a literal spatial rendering that does not capture the meaning.
'популярный' means popular; 'well-known' means famous or recognized and does not fully capture popularity.
In English 'genius' as a predicate noun requires the article 'a'; 'is genius' without the article is ungrammatical.

ok: He performs on a big stage.
bad: He comes out on a big scene.
why: 'выступает на сцене' is 'performs on stage'; 'scene' in English is a part of a play, not the physical stage platform.

ok: The novel was written in the 19th century.
bad: The roman was written in the XIX century.
why: 'роман' is 'novel' in English; 'roman' is the French and Russian term. Roman numerals should be written as ordinals: '19th century', not 'XIX century'.

bad: He removed himself in the cinema.
why: 'снялся' in film context means appeared in or starred in a film; 'removed himself' is a literal rendering of the reflexive 'сняться'.
'аплодировали стоя' is the equivalent of a standing ovation; 'applauded while standing' misses the idiomatic expression.

ok: I listen to jazz on headphones.
why: 'слушаю' means listen to (actively); 'hear' is passive perception; 'in headphones' should be 'on headphones' or 'through headphones'.

ok: This is a classic of the genre.
bad: This is a classic of the type.
why: 'жанр' is the French-derived word 'genre'; 'type' is a generic English word that loses the specific literary/artistic meaning.
'рисует' means draws (pencil, pen, sketch); 'paints' specifically means using paint, which is a narrower and potentially incorrect meaning.
'получилась' means came out or turned out; 'resulted blurred' is a literal and ungrammatical rendering.
'занимается' in an arts context means works with or creates; 'is engaged in' is overly formal and sounds like bureaucratic language.
'с нетерпением' is idiomatically 'eagerly' or 'impatiently'; 'with impatience' is a literal rendering that sounds dated.

ok: The song made it into the charts.
bad: The song fell into the charts.
why: 'попала в чарты' means entered the charts; 'fell into the charts' implies dropping, which is the opposite of the intended meaning.

ok: I signed up for drawing classes.
bad: I wrote myself on drawing courses.
why: 'записался на курсы' means signed up for classes; 'wrote myself on courses' is a literal rendering of the reflexive verb.

src: Она выиграла первое место на конкурсе.
ok: She won first place in the competition.
bad: She earned first place at the concourse.
why: 'конкурс' is a competition or contest; 'concourse' is a large open area in a station or airport and is a false cognate.
Art movements are proper nouns and require capitalisation in English; 'impressionism' without a capital is incorrect.
'фальшиво' in music means out of tune; 'falsely' means dishonestly or incorrectly in a different sense and is not used for singing.
'impressive' is the correct adjective; 'impressing' as a predicate adjective is ungrammatical in this context.
'вживую' means live (as in a live performance); 'alive' is a false friend that means living and not dead.
'не попал на' means missed or didn't make it to; 'didn't hit the premiere' is a literal and unnatural rendering.

bad: The staging was on the highest level.
why: 'на высшем уровне' is the idiom 'top-notch' or 'of the highest standard'; 'on the highest level' is a literal rendering.
'стихи' can be either poems or poetry; 'poetry' is more natural when speaking of it as a form of art generally.

ok: The film was shot in black and white.
bad: The cinema was filmed in black-white.
why: 'кино' here means a film, not the cinema building; 'black and white' needs the conjunction 'and'.

bad: She dances on a professional level.
why: 'professionally' is the concise adverb; 'on a professional level' is verbose and overly formal for describing a dancer.

bad: He is engaged in painting pictures.
why: The rejected translation adds 'pictures' which is not in the source and is overly verbose; 'he paints' is the natural English equivalent.
'спектакль' is a theatrical performance; 'spectacle' in English means an impressive or dramatic sight, not a theatre show.

bad: I read the book while swallowing.
why: 'взахлёб' is an idiom meaning greedily or non-stop; 'while swallowing' is an absurd literal rendering.
'были в восторге' is the idiom 'were thrilled' or 'were delighted'; 'were in delight' is a literal rendering of the prepositional structure.
In English instrument playing uses 'the' before the instrument name; 'plays on guitar' omits the required article.

bad: The film has a cult's status.
why: 'cult status' is a fixed noun phrase in English; 'a cult's status' uses a possessive that changes the meaning.

ok: She likes to read before bed.
bad: She loves reading before falling into sleep.
why: 'перед сном' is 'before bed' or 'before sleeping'; 'before falling into sleep' is an unnatural literal rendering.

ok: The painting is on display in the museum.
bad: The picture is exhibited in museum.
why: 'in museum' is missing the required definite article; it should be 'in the museum'.
'снял фильм' in filmmaking means made a film; 'removed a film' is a literal rendering of 'снять' in its physical sense.

bad: It was an unforgettable staging of the play.
why: The rejected translation adds 'of the play' which is not in the source and makes the sentence unnecessarily verbose.

ok: We're going on vacation in the summer.
bad: We ride on vacation in summer.
why: 'едем в отпуск' means going on vacation; 'ride' implies a vehicle and does not capture the general meaning of travelling.

ok: You need your passport at boarding.
why: 'посадка' in aviation is boarding; 'planting' is a literal mistranslation of the verb 'сажать'.

ok: The flight is delayed by two hours.
bad: The flight is late on two hours.
why: In English delays use the preposition 'by'; 'late on two hours' is an ungrammatical construction.

src: Я взял номер с видом на море.
ok: I booked a room with a sea view.
bad: I took a room with a view on the sea.
why: 'вид на море' is 'sea view' or 'ocean view'; 'view on the sea' uses a wrong preposition and is not the standard compound noun.

ok: We got lost in an unfamiliar city.
bad: We lost ourselves in an unknown city.
why: 'потерялись' means got lost; 'lost ourselves' is an unnatural reflexive rendering, and 'unknown' does not capture the nuance of 'незнакомый' (unfamiliar to us).

bad: In hotel there is good servicing.
why: 'обслуживание' means service; 'servicing' implies mechanical maintenance and is not used for hotel hospitality.

bad: We took a car for rental.
why: 'взяли напрокат машину' is 'rented a car'; 'took a car for rental' is verbose and non-idiomatic.

ok: The visa has already been approved.
why: 'одобрена' means approved; 'confirmed' is used for bookings and appointments, not for visa status.
'экскурсия' in everyday tourism context is 'tour'; 'excursion' is understood but sounds formal and is less common in English.
'загорелыми' means tanned from the sun; 'burned' implies sunburn which is a negative outcome and a different meaning.

ok: We were given a table by the window.
bad: To us was given a table near the window.
why: 'by the window' is the standard English phrase; 'to us was given' is a literal dative rendering with awkward word order.

ok: The tourists were photographing the sights.
bad: The tourists photographed the remarkable places.
why: 'достопримечательности' is 'sights' or 'attractions'; 'remarkable places' is a clumsy literal translation of the compound word.

src: Мы поехали на экскурсию в горы.
ok: We went on a trip to the mountains.
bad: We went on excursion in mountains.
why: 'on a trip to the mountains' requires the articles; 'on excursion in mountains' omits both articles incorrectly.
'кухня' in this context means cuisine; 'kitchen' is the room for cooking, which is a false cognate error.

src: Путешествовать — это лучший способ познавать мир.
ok: Travelling is the best way to discover the world.
bad: To travel — this is the best way to know the world.
why: The infinitive construction with dash and 'это' should become a gerund subject; 'to know the world' is also less natural than 'discover the world'.

ok: They vacationed at the seaside for a week.
bad: They rested at sea for one week.
why: 'отдыхали на море' means holidaying at the seaside; 'rested at sea' implies being on a ship and is not idiomatic.
English negation requires the auxiliary verb 'didn't'; 'baggage not came' is an ungrammatical construction.

ok: We bought souvenirs for our family.
why: 'сувениры' means souvenirs (keepsakes); 'memories' is an incorrect translation, and 'relatives' is more formal than 'family'.

ok: The hotel is in the city centre.
bad: The hotel is situated in the center of the city.
why: 'is situated' is a formal passive; in everyday English 'is in the city centre' is more natural and less verbose.
'вовремя' means on time (punctually); 'in time' means with time to spare before a deadline, which is a different meaning.

bad: On the beach was much people.
why: 'много народу' means the place was crowded; 'much people' is ungrammatical — 'people' takes 'many' not 'much', and the subject-verb agreement is wrong.
'остановился' in accommodation context means stayed; 'stopped' implies a brief physical halt and is not the correct term for staying overnight.

ok: The train departs from platform three.
bad: The train departs from the third way.
why: 'путь' in railway context is 'platform' or 'track'; 'the third way' is a literal translation that is meaningless in this context.
'маршрут' is 'route' in English; 'marshroute' is a non-existent word combining Russian and English.

bad: We took bicycles for hire to us.
why: 'взяли напрокат' means rented; 'took for hire to us' is a clumsy literal rendering of the Russian phrase.
'таможня прошла' means going through customs went smoothly; 'the customs was fast' treats customs as a singular entity and is less natural.

src: Мы ехали четыре часа без остановок.
ok: We drove for four hours without stops.
bad: We went four hours without stoppings.
why: 'stoppings' is not a valid English noun form; 'stops' is the correct plural.
'гостиница' is a hotel; 'guesthouse' is a smaller accommodation type and is not interchangeable in all contexts.
'приветливы' means friendly or welcoming; 'were greeting' is a wrong verb form — 'greeting' is a participle not a predicate adjective.
'speak a language' is the standard collocation; 'talks on' is an incorrect preposition usage.
'набережная' is a waterfront promenade; 'embankment' in English typically refers to a raised bank alongside a river, not a promenade.

bad: I am reserving the hotel in online.
why: 'in online' is ungrammatical; 'online' is an adverb and does not take a preposition.

ok: The trip turned out to be unforgettable.
why: 'оказалась' means turned out to be; 'resulted unforgettable' is ungrammatical — 'result in' cannot be followed by a bare adjective.
'ухабистой' means bumpy; 'hump-filled' is not a standard English adjective.

ok: We got lost in the forest.
bad: We lost our way in the wood.
why: 'заблудились' means got lost; 'lost our way' is correct but 'got lost' is more natural in conversational English.

ok: We were held up at the border.
bad: We were delayed on the border.
why: In English 'at the border' is the standard prepositional phrase; 'on the border' means situated along the border rather than passing through it.

bad: The rest passed with a hurrah.
why: 'на ура' is an idiom meaning excellently or with great success; 'with a hurrah' is a literal rendering that does not convey the meaning.

src: У нас была пересадка в Стамбуле.
ok: We had a layover in Istanbul.
bad: We had a transfer in Istanbul.
why: 'пересадка' in air travel is a 'layover' or 'stopover'; 'transfer' is used more for ground transport connections.

bad: I am already in the path.
why: 'в пути' is the idiom 'on my way'; 'in the path' is a literal rendering of the prepositional phrase.

ok: The mountains were covered in snow.
bad: The mountains were covered by snow.
why: 'covered in snow' is the standard collocation in English for surfaces blanketed with snow; 'covered by snow' implies the snow acted as an agent.
'осмотрели' in a tourist context means explored or visited; 'examined' implies close inspection and is formal, not the word used for sightseeing.
'безлюдным' is the adjective 'deserted'; 'without people' is a literal rendering that misses the single English word.

ok: We brought rain jackets with us.
bad: We took with us rain coats.
why: 'дождевик' is a rain jacket or raincoat; the word order in the rejected translation is awkward.

ok: Boarding was announced at gate twenty.
bad: The boarding was declared on exit twenty.
why: 'выход' in an airport is a gate; 'exit' means a way out of a building, not an airport departure gate.

ok: Prices in tourist areas are inflated.
bad: Prices in tourism places are overraised.
why: 'завышены' means inflated or overpriced; 'overraised' is not a standard English word.

ok: We watched the sunrise from the summit.
bad: We met the sunrise on the top.
why: 'встретили рассвет' is idiomatically 'watched the sunrise'; 'met the sunrise' is a literal translation that does not work in English.
'раньше расписания' is the idiom 'ahead of schedule'; 'before the timetable' is a literal rendering that does not work in English.

ok: We had to sit in traffic for a long time.
bad: It was necessary to stand long in a stopper.
why: 'стоять в пробке' is 'stuck in traffic' or 'sit in traffic'; 'stand in a stopper' is a literal and nonsensical rendering.

bad: I need a map of city.
why: 'of city' is missing the definite article; it should be 'of the city' or more naturally 'a city map'.
'провели' here means spent (time); 'carried' is a literal translation of 'проводить' in its physical sense.
'провалил' for exams or interviews means failed; 'fell through' means a plan collapsed, not that a person failed a test.

ok: The salary is paid once a month.
bad: The salary is payed once in month.
why: 'payed' is an incorrect past participle; the correct form is 'paid'. 'once in month' also requires the article 'a'.
'сверхурочно' is the established English word 'overtime'; 'over hours' is a literal rendering that does not exist as a set phrase.

ok: He was fired for being late.
why: 'latenesses' is not a standard English noun form; 'being late' or 'tardiness' are the correct expressions.
'повышение' in a career context means promotion (a higher position); 'raise' means a salary increase, which is a different meaning.
'deadline' is a single compound word in English; 'dead line' (two words) is incorrect.

bad: We held a planning meeting in the morning.
why: 'планёрка' is a short status meeting; the rejected translation adds 'planning' which implies a longer strategy session and misrepresents the original.
'работает на себя' means self-employed or works for himself; 'works on himself' means self-improvement, which is a different meaning.

ok: We need to align on the details.
bad: We need to agree the details.
why: 'согласовать' in a business context is 'align on' or 'finalize'; 'agree the details' is used in British English but 'agree on' or 'align on' is more standard.
'announced about' is redundant; the correct collocation is 'announced bankruptcy' or 'declared bankruptcy'.
'больничный' colloquially means sick leave; 'sick-list' is a literal translation of the document name, not the English term for the leave itself.

ok: We're working on a new project.
bad: We work above a new project.
why: 'работаем над' means working on; 'above' is an incorrect preposition — the correct preposition is 'on'.

ok: She works seven days a week.
why: 'без выходных' means without days off; the idiomatic English equivalent is 'seven days a week' or 'without days off'.

bad: We need a qualified specialist person.
why: The rejected translation adds 'person' which is redundant since 'specialist' already refers to a person.
'готов' in a formal work context is 'ready' or 'complete'; 'done' is casual and can imply the task is finished but the report may not be polished.
'справился' in professional contexts is most naturally 'handled' or 'completed'; 'coped' implies struggling under difficulty, which changes the tone.

ok: The contract has been signed by both parties.
bad: The contract is signed by the two sides.
why: 'сторонами' in legal context is 'parties'; 'sides' implies a dispute, and 'the two sides' is not the standard legal phrasing.

ok: I'm up to my neck in work.
bad: I am busy up to the throat.
why: 'занят по горло' is a Russian idiom; the English equivalent is 'up to my neck in work', not the literal 'up to the throat'.

bad: The negotiations went into a deaf corner.
why: 'тупик' is a deadlock or impasse; 'deaf corner' is a nonsensical literal translation of the Russian word 'тупик'.

ok: I need to clarify the task.
bad: I need to precise the task.
why: 'уточнить' means clarify or specify; 'to precise' is not a standard English verb — 'precise' is an adjective.
'canceled' uses single-l American spelling; 'cancelled' (double-l) is the standard British spelling consistent with the domain; the present perfect 'has been cancelled' is also more precise.

ok: He is responsible for the department.
bad: He carries responsibility for the department.
why: 'несёт ответственность' is idiomatically 'is responsible for'; 'carries responsibility' is a literal rendering of the verb 'нести'.
'упала' means dropped or fell; 'fell down' is redundant — 'fell' alone or 'dropped' is the correct phrasing.

bad: We need to conduct a brain storm.
why: 'мозговой штурм' is the Russian borrowing of 'brainstorm'; 'brain storm' (two words) is incorrect and 'conduct' is unnecessarily formal.

bad: He copes himself with stress well.
why: 'справляется' does not require a reflexive pronoun in English; 'copes himself' is an unnatural literal rendering.
'закрыли сделку' is the business idiom 'closed the deal'; 'shut the deal' does not exist as an idiom in English.

bad: He always goes away before time.
why: 'раньше времени' means early or ahead of time; 'before time' is a literal rendering that sounds unnatural.

ok: The resume needs to be updated.
bad: The summary needs to be updated.
why: 'резюме' in a professional job context is 'resume' (CV); 'summary' is a general English word meaning a condensed version, which is a false cognate in this context.

ok: The task was completed on time.
bad: The task was fulfilled in the term.
why: 'выполнена в срок' means completed on time; 'fulfilled in the term' is a literal rendering where 'срок' is mistranslated as 'term'.
'resources' is a countable noun that requires the plural form here; 'resource' (singular) is incorrect.
'коллектив' is most naturally 'team' in English; 'collective' has political connotations, and 'coordinated' does not capture the Russian nuance of harmony.
'ведёт переговоры' means conducting negotiations; 'leads negotiations' implies heading a negotiation team, which is a different sense.

ok: The office is on the fifth floor.
bad: The office is on fifth floor.
why: 'on the fifth floor' requires the definite article; 'on fifth floor' omits the required article.
'запустили' in a business context means launched; 'started a product' is not an established English business phrase.

bad: He went away from the company.
why: 'ушёл из компании' means left the company; 'went away from the company' is a literal rendering that sounds unnatural.

bad: I am in a business trip.
why: 'on a business trip' is the correct English preposition; 'in a business trip' is an incorrect preposition choice.

ok: The three of us were invited to the meeting.
bad: Us three were invited to meeting.
why: 'Us three' is incorrect; English uses 'the three of us' as the subject; 'to meeting' also omits the required article.
'остался доволен' is idiomatically 'was satisfied' or 'was happy'; 'remained content' is overly literary for a business context.

ok: We need to stay within budget.
bad: We need to fit inside the budget.
why: 'уложиться в бюджет' is the idiom 'stay within budget'; 'fit inside the budget' is a literal rendering that is not idiomatic.

bad: He pulls the blanket on himself.
why: 'тянет одеяло на себя' is an idiom meaning to take all the credit or glory; 'pulls the blanket on himself' is the literal rendering that does not convey the idiom.

ok: The project was completed ahead of schedule.
bad: The project was finished before term.
why: 'досрочно' means ahead of schedule; 'before term' is a literal rendering of the Russian word 'срок'.

ok: Employees work on a flexible schedule.
bad: Employees work in a flexible graph.
why: 'график' in work scheduling is 'schedule'; 'graph' is the visual data representation, which is a false cognate error.

bad: We talked over all the questions.
why: 'вопросы' in a meeting context means issues or agenda items; 'questions' implies literal interrogative questions rather than business topics.
'выговор' in employment is a formal reprimand or written warning; 'call-out' in British English can mean a public criticism on social media, not a formal HR action.

bad: We signed a collaboration agreement about cooperation.
why: The rejected translation is redundant: 'collaboration agreement about cooperation' repeats the concept twice; 'cooperation agreement' or 'partnership agreement' is sufficient.

ok: He sets the tone for the team.
bad: He gives the tone in the team.
why: 'задаёт тон' is 'sets the tone'; 'gives the tone' is not an established idiom in English.

ok: The probationary period is three months.
bad: The test period is three months.
why: 'испытательный срок' is the HR term 'probationary period'; 'test period' is a literal rendering that is not the standard employment phrase.
'ищем' in English is 'looking for'; 'search for' is used for more intensive or physical searching, not the standard business phrasing.
Growth or increase in English uses 'by' to indicate the amount; 'on' is an incorrect preposition here.

bad: The team worked in a well-coordinated manner.
why: 'слаженно' is best rendered as 'seamlessly' or 'in sync'; 'in a well-coordinated manner' is overly formal and bureaucratic for describing teamwork.
